2.2.20.9: As soon as I touched my own head with my own hand, at that very moment the form of that bull-rider Śiva was immediately established there. ॥9॥
2.2.20.10: Then, my limbs overcome with shame, I stood with downcast face, clearly seen by all the immortals headed by Indra, who stood all around. ॥10॥
2.2.20.11: Then, filled with shame, I prostrated before Maheśvara, offered praise, and said: Forgive me, forgive me. ॥11॥
2.2.20.12: For the purification of this sin, tell me an expiation, O lord, and likewise a just punishment, by which my sin may depart. ॥12॥
2.2.20.13: Thus addressed by me, Śambhu, the lord of all, affectionate to devotees, becoming even more pleased, spoke to me as I bowed. ॥13॥
2.2.20.14: Śambhu said: In this very form, presided over by me, perform austerity with a serene mind, devoted to my worship. ॥14॥
2.2.20.15: You will attain fame everywhere on earth by the name Rudraśiras, as the accomplisher of all the tasks of the brilliant twice-born. ॥15॥
2.2.20.16: Since this act—your shedding of semen just now—is a deed of humans, therefore you, becoming a human, will wander upon the earth. ॥16॥
2.2.20.17: And whoever on earth, seeing you in this form, goes about saying, what is this on Brahmā's head?—so spoke the Destroyer of the Cities— ॥17॥
2.2.20.18: and who then, out of curiosity, hears all your conduct—he, through that renunciation, will at once attain release from the sin committed with others' wives. ॥18॥
2.2.20.19: The more people proclaim this deed of yours, the more will you be purified of this sin. ॥19॥
2.2.20.20: This indeed, O Brahmā, is the expiation declared by me for you: making you a laughing-stock among people in the world and a source of supreme reproach to you. ॥20॥
2.2.20.21: And this semen of yours, afflicted by lust, which fell in the middle of the altar, has been seen by me; it will not be retained. ॥21॥
2.2.20.22: Your semen, measuring four drops, which fell upon the ground—clouds of that number, bringing about dissolution, shall arise in the sky. ॥22॥
2.2.20.23: Meanwhile, right there before the divine sages, clouds of that number quickly arose from that semen. ॥23॥
2.2.20.24: Saṃvartaka, Āvarta, Puṣkara and Droṇa—these, dear one, are the four kinds of great clouds that bring about dissolution. ॥24॥
2.2.20.25: Then, thundering and releasing water slightly by Śiva's will, those clouds with harsh roars spread across the sky, O best of sages. ॥25॥
2.2.20.26: When the sky was covered by those loudly thundering clouds, Śaṅkara, calmed by the goddess Dākṣāyaṇī, quickly became completely peaceful. ॥26॥
2.2.20.27: Then I, freed from fear, at Śaṅkara's command, brought the remaining marriage rites to completion, O sage. ॥27॥
2.2.20.28: A shower of flowers, joyfully released by the hosts of gods, fell on the heads of Śivā and Śiva and everywhere, O best of sages. ॥28॥
2.2.20.29: While instruments were being played and they were singing, and while groups of brahmins, filled with devotion, were reciting the Vedas, ॥29॥
2.2.20.30: and while Rambhā and other ladies were dancing with zeal, there was a great festival among the wives of the gods, O Nārada. ॥30॥
2.2.20.31: Then the Supreme Lord, master of the performance of rites, pleased and adopting worldly custom, lovingly addressed me as I stood with joined palms. ॥31॥
2.2.20.32: Īśvara said: O Brahmā, the entire marriage rite has been well performed. I am pleased. You are the officiating priest; what fee shall I give you? ॥32॥
2.2.20.33: Ask for it, O eldest of the gods, even if it be very hard to obtain. Speak quickly, O greatly fortunate one; nothing exists that I cannot give. ॥33॥
2.2.20.34: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Śaṅkara, I, with joined palms and humble mind, bowing to the Lord again and again, said, O sage: ॥34॥
2.2.20.35: If you are pleased, O lord of gods, and if I am worthy of a boon, then, O Maheśāna, do with great love what I say. ॥35॥
2.2.20.36: In this very form, O Maheśvara, you should always remain here on this altar, for the purification of men's sins. ॥36॥
2.2.20.37: So that, having made my own hermitage near it, O moon-crested one, I may perform austerity for the destruction of this sin of mine, O Śaṅkara. ॥37॥
2.2.20.38: Whatever man on earth beholds you with devotion on the thirteenth day of the bright half of Caitra, under the asterism presided over by Bhaga, on a Sunday— ॥38॥
2.2.20.39: at that very moment may his sins go to destruction, O Hara; may abundant merit increase, and may diseases perish entirely. ॥39॥
2.2.20.40: Whatever woman is ill-fated, barren, one-eyed or devoid of beauty—she too, merely by seeing you, would surely become free of defects. ॥40॥
2.2.20.41: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of mine, which brought every happiness to his own self, Śiva said with a very pleased mind, so be it. ॥41॥
2.2.20.42: Śiva said: For the welfare of all the world, O Brahmā (Vidhi), at your word I shall remain stationed on that altar together with my wife Satī. ॥42॥
2.2.20.43: Brahmā said: Having said this, the blessed bull-bannered Lord, with his wife, standing in the middle of the altar and having made a form that was a portion of himself, spoke. ॥43॥
2.2.20.44: Then Śaṅkara, the Supreme Lord, affectionate to his own people, having taken leave of Dakṣa, became intent on departing with his wife Satī. ॥44॥
2.2.20.45: Meanwhile the wise Dakṣa, bowed down in humility, with joined palms and bending low, lovingly praised the bull-bannered Lord. ॥45॥
2.2.20.46: Then all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, the sages and the gaṇas, having bowed and praised him in many ways, joyfully raised cries of victory. ॥46॥
2.2.20.47: Having joyfully placed Satī on the bull with Dakṣa's permission, Śambhu, the Lord himself, seated on the bull, went to the plateau of Himavat. ॥47॥
2.2.20.48: Then she, fair-toothed and sweetly smiling, seated on the bull beside Śaṅkara, shone like a dark streak near the moon. ॥48॥
2.2.20.49: All the gods headed by Viṣṇu, likewise the seers headed by Marīci, and Dakṣa too were enchanted, and the other people likewise stood motionless. ॥49॥
2.2.20.50: Some, playing instruments, and others, singing melodiously Śiva's pure and auspicious glory, joyfully followed Śiva. ॥50॥
2.2.20.51: Then Dakṣa, lovingly dismissed by Śambhu midway along the road, returned to his own abode; Śambhu, with his gaṇas, was overcome with love. ॥51॥
2.2.20.52: Though dismissed by Śambhu, those gods headed by Viṣṇu again followed Śiva with devotion and supreme joy. ॥52॥
2.2.20.53: Accompanied by all of them and his gaṇas, and by Satī his own wife, Śambhu, delighted, reached his own abode, beautified by the Himavat mountain. ॥53॥
2.2.20.54: Having gone there, he joyfully bade farewell to all the gods, the sages and the others as well, after honouring them greatly and respectfully. ॥54॥
2.2.20.55: Having spoken to Śambhu, all of them—the sages and gods headed by Viṣṇu—with joyful faces, bowed and praised him and went each to his own abode. ॥55॥
2.2.20.56: Śiva too, exceedingly delighted, dwelling on the plateau of Himavat, sported with his wife, the daughter of Dakṣa, conforming to worldly ways. ॥56॥
2.2.20.57: Then, O sage, that Śaṅkara, the maker of creation, with Satī and his gaṇas, delighted, reached his own abode Kailāsa, the best of mountains. ॥57॥
2.2.20.58: All this has been told to you, how the marriage of the bull-riding Lord took place long ago, in the Manu-period of Svāyambhuva. ॥58॥
2.2.20.59: Whoever, at the time of a marriage, at a sacrifice, or at the start of any undertaking, having worshipped the bull-bannered Lord, listens attentively to this narrative— ॥59॥
2.2.20.60: —for him every marriage rite will be free of obstacles, and any other auspicious rite will always be unimpeded. ॥60॥
2.2.20.61: And a maiden who lovingly hears this auspicious narrative will be endowed with happiness, good fortune, virtue, good conduct and fine qualities, and will become a chaste wife blessed with sons. ॥61॥
2.2.20.iti: Thus ends the twentieth adhyāya, named The marriage of Satī, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥20॥
2.2.21.1: Nārada said: Your words are excellent, dear father, O sinless one, since you know everything. We have indeed heard the most wondrous and auspicious story of Śiva and Śivā. ॥1॥
2.2.21.2: The marriage too has been heard in full: it removes all delusion, is filled with supreme knowledge, and is the excellent abode of auspiciousness. ॥2॥
2.2.21.3: Yet I wish to know still more of the auspicious story of Śiva and Śivā. So, O greatly wise one, showing your matchless compassion, describe it readily. ॥3॥
2.2.21.4: Brahmā said: Your inquiry, O sage, befits one who is truly compassionate, since by it I have been urged, O gentle one, to narrate Śiva's divine play. ॥4॥
2.2.21.5: Learn from me what Śiva did with great joy after marrying the goddess Satī, Dakṣa's daughter and mother of the three worlds, and going to his own abode. ॥5॥
2.2.21.6: Then Hara, with his attendants, reached his delightful abode, O divine sage, and there dismounted from his beloved bull. ॥6॥
2.2.21.7: Entering his own abode as was fitting, Śiva, Satī's companion, who follows worldly conduct, rejoiced exceedingly, O divine sage. ॥7॥
2.2.21.8: Then Virūpākṣa, having obtained this daughter of Dakṣa, sent his own attendants, Nandin and the others, out of the mountain cave. ॥8॥
2.2.21.9: And the Lord, an ocean of compassion, following worldly custom, spoke very kindly to all of them, Nandin and the rest. ॥9॥
2.2.21.10: Maheśa said: Whenever I remember you here, my attendants, come quickly to my side, your minds intent on my remembrance. ॥10॥
2.2.21.11: When Vāmadeva had said this, Nandin and the others, his own attendants, very swift and very heroic, went off to various places. ॥11॥
2.2.21.12: When they had gone, the Lord too, playful, sported with her, the daughter of Dakṣa, in seclusion, greatly delighted. ॥12॥
2.2.21.13: Sometimes he gathered wild flowers, made a charming garland, and placed it on Satī where a necklace would lie. ॥13॥
2.2.21.14: Sometimes, when Satī was looking at herself in a mirror, Hara came up behind her and looked at his own face too. ॥14॥
2.2.21.15: Sometimes, close beside her, he would toss her earring again and again, fasten it and unfasten it, and she herself would set it right. ॥15॥
2.2.21.16: Vṛṣadhvaja made her feet, already naturally red, fully red with bright lac. ॥16॥
2.2.21.17: Even things that could be said aloud before others, Hara would whisper at length in her ear, so as to see her face. ॥17॥
2.2.21.18: Having gone not even far, he would come back carefully and embrace from behind the fair-eyed one while her mind was elsewhere. ॥18॥
2.2.21.19: Vṛṣabhadhvaja, having vanished right there by his magic, embraced her; startled with fear, she became agitated. ॥19॥
2.2.21.20: On her two breasts, like golden lotus buds, he drew a musk ornament in the shape of a bee. ॥20॥
2.2.21.21: Hara suddenly removed the necklace from her breasts and put it back in the same place, touching her again and again with his hand. ॥21॥
2.2.21.22: Again and again he loosened her armlets, bracelets and rings, and then put them back in their places. ॥22॥
2.2.21.23: He would say, your friend Kālikā, of like complexion, is coming here; and as she looked thus, he would boldly go for her lofty breasts. ॥23॥
2.2.21.24: Sometimes the lord of the Pramathas, his mind maddened by love, made jests and delights, and his beloved did likewise with joy. ॥24॥
2.2.21.25: Gathering lotuses and other lovely flowers, Śaṅkara lovingly made flower ornaments for all her limbs. ॥25॥
2.2.21.26: Maheśvara, kind to his devotees, roamed with his beloved Satī through all the lovely mountain bowers. ॥26॥
2.2.21.27: Without her he would not go anywhere, would not stay, would not act; without her Śaṅkara found no ease even for a moment. ॥27॥
2.2.21.28: Having sported for a very long time on Kailāsa, the best of mountains, he went to the Himālaya's slopes and of his own will called Smara Kāma to mind. ॥28॥
2.2.21.29: When Kāma had entered, Spring, near Śaṅkara, spread forth his own nature, knowing what was in the Lord's heart. ॥29॥
2.2.21.30: All the trees blossomed, and the creepers and other plants blossomed too; the waters had full-blown lotuses, and the lotuses were alive with bees. ॥30॥
2.2.21.31: When that fine season had arrived there, the Malaya breeze blew, delightful and fragrant with the scent of sweet-smelling flowers. ॥31॥
2.2.21.32: The palāśa blossoms shone like the crescent moon at twilight, and the flowers on the trees, like Kāma's weapons, shone with gladness. ॥32॥
2.2.21.33: Lotus flowers shone in the lakes; the fair-faced wind-goddess set about bewildering all people. ॥33॥
2.2.21.34: Near Śaṅkara the nāgakeśara trees, lovely with golden blossoms, shone like the banners of Madana. ॥34॥
2.2.21.35: The clove creeper, perfuming the breeze with its sweet fragrance, greatly bewitched the hearts of lovers then. ॥35॥
2.2.21.36: The mango trees, adorned with swarms of bees and resounding sweetly, shone, pervaded by Madana, as though a couch for his host of arrows. ॥36॥
2.2.21.37: The stainless waters with blooming lotuses shone like the minds of sages in which the light of the Self has clearly arisen. ॥37॥
2.2.21.38: The frosts, meeting the sun's rays, departed; and then beings were seen intoxicated, their hearts melted like water. ॥38॥
2.2.21.39: Then the nights, clear and free of mist, became lovely with the moon, just as charming women are with their beloved. ॥39॥
2.2.21.40: At that time Mahādeva sported with Satī on that best of mountains for a very long time, as he pleased, in the bowers and by the rivers. ॥40॥
2.2.21.41: O sage, Dākṣāyaṇī then shone together with him in such a way that Hara could not find peace even for a moment without her. ॥41॥
2.2.21.42: In the matter of love's enjoyment, the goddess Satī, dear to his heart, seemed as it were to enter into Hara's body, as though making him drink that delight. ॥42॥
2.2.21.43: Adorning her whole body with flower garlands made by his own hands, he created ever new delight. ॥43॥
2.2.21.44: Through chats, glances, laughter and conversations Hara instructed Girijā, as though proclaiming to her the knowledge of the Self. ॥44॥
2.2.21.45: Hara, his body made steady by drinking the nectar of the moon of her face, at times entered a subtle state marked by manifold distinctions. ॥45॥
2.2.21.46: By the fragrance of her lotus face, by her beauty and her playful jests, he was bound like a great tusked elephant by ropes, with no other activity. ॥46॥
2.2.21.47: Thus, on the slopes and in the bowers of the Himālaya and in its caves, Maheśa sported every day with Dakṣa's daughter. While he played, O divine sage, ten and ten and five more years passed, measured by the reckoning of the gods. ॥47॥
2.2.21.iti: Thus ends the twenty-first adhyāya, named The play of Satī and Śiva, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥21॥
2.2.22.1: Brahmā said: Then once, when the rainy season had come, Dakṣa's daughter spoke to the bull-bannered Śiva, who was staying on a plateau of Mount Kailāsa. ॥1॥
2.2.22.2: Satī said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, Śambhu, beloved of my life, listen to my words, O Lord, and having heard them, act on them, O giver of honour. ॥2॥
2.2.22.3: This rainy season has arrived, a time most hard to bear; masses of clouds of many colours make the sky and the regions of the quarters resound. ॥3॥
2.2.22.4: Swift winds blow, as if captivating the heart, washed with kadamba pollen and carrying along drops of water. ॥4॥
2.2.22.5: Whose mind would not be agitated by the loud, fierce thunderings of the clouds that pour down torrents of rain and bear lightning as their banners? ॥5॥
2.2.22.6: The sun is not seen, nor the moon, which is covered by clouds; even by day it looks like night, a source of anguish to those separated from their beloved. ॥6॥
2.2.22.7: O Śaṅkara, the clouds, never staying in one place, thundering and driven by the winds, seem as if they are falling upon people's heads. ॥7॥
2.2.22.8: O Hara, great trees struck by the wind appear as if dancing in the sky, frightening to the timid yet longed for by lovers. ॥8॥
2.2.22.9: Behind the mass of clouds, glossy like dark-blue collyrium, the line of cranes shines very high, like foam on the surface of the Yamunā. ॥9॥
2.2.22.10: At night, O Lord, rings of lightning are seen clinging to the elephant-like clouds, like the blazing submarine fire Vaḍavāmukha in the ocean. ॥10॥
2.2.22.11: Here on Mandara crops are sprouting even in the courtyards; what then shall I say, O Virūpākṣa, of the growth of crops elsewhere? ॥11॥
2.2.22.12: This Himālaya is bright with dark, silvery and red hues; the mass of clouds resting on Mandara, with its leaf-like patches, looks like the ocean of milk. ॥12॥
2.2.22.13: And incomparable splendour has crookedly resorted to the kiṃśuka trees, high and low, just as in the Kali age Lakṣmī will go to the unworthy, abandoning good people. ॥13॥
2.2.22.14: Delighted again and again by the sound of the clouds on Mount Mandara, the peacocks keep crying kekā in every forest, displaying their tail-plumes. ॥14॥
2.2.22.15: Sweet and charming is the call of the cātaka birds yearning for the clouds; the arrows of torrential rain have fallen upon the heat that rose from every path. ॥15॥
2.2.22.16: See the misconduct of the clouds on my body with showers of hailstones. They pelt even the peacocks and cātakas who follow them. ॥16॥
2.2.22.17: Seeing the humiliation of the peacock and the cātaka even at the hands of their friend, O Giriśa, the swans joyfully go even to faraway Mānasa. ॥17॥
2.2.22.18: In this harsh season even crows and cakoras build nests; without a house, how will you find peace? ॥18॥
2.2.22.19: Today a great fear born of the clouds has seized me, O bearer of Pināka; therefore, at my word, strive without delay for a dwelling. ॥19॥
2.2.22.20: Whether on Kailāsa, on the Himālaya, or at Mahākośī on earth, make a suitable dwelling there, O bull-bannered one. ॥20॥
2.2.22.21: Brahmā said: Addressed thus repeatedly by her, Dākṣāyaṇī, Śambhu laughed, his face an abode of smiles lit by the rays of the moon on his head. ॥21॥
2.2.22.22: Then the great-souled Supreme Lord, knower of all principles, his lips parted in a smile, spoke to the goddess Satī, pleasing her. ॥22॥
2.2.22.23: Īśvara said: O charming one, my beloved, where I shall make a dwelling for your pleasure, there clouds will never go. ॥23॥
2.2.22.24: O charming one, the clouds always move only as far as the slopes of the snow-peaked mountain, even in the rains. ॥24॥
2.2.22.25: Likewise, O goddess, the clouds mostly move about the foot of Kailāsa; they never go above it. ॥25॥
2.2.22.26: Nor do the clouds Puṣkara, Āvartaka and the rest go above Mount Sumeru; they reach only the root of the Jambū tree. ॥26॥
2.2.22.27: Among these lords of mountains I have named, on whichever your heart desires to dwell, tell me that quickly. ॥27॥
2.2.22.28: On the snow-born mountain, your delights in roaming at will shall be joyfully sung by flocks upon flocks of golden-winged birds and by the winds, with those sweet notes rising in waves of sound. ॥28॥
2.2.22.29: The Siddha women, having prepared seats for you, long for you on the ground, eagerly offering gifts; on the mountain with jewelled floors, during your free roaming, they serve you and will wish to honour you with gifts of fruits and the like. ॥29॥
2.2.22.30: The daughters of the serpent-lords, the mountain maidens, the Nāga maidens and the chief horse-faced women—all of them will constantly assist you with charming gestures of delight. ॥30॥
2.2.22.31: Seeing your incomparable form and lovely face, those women, beautiful with unblinking eyes, will ever hold in disdain their own bodies and the charms of their own beauty. ॥31॥
2.2.22.32: Menakā, the wife of the king of mountains, renowned in the three worlds for her beauty and virtues, she too will always delight your mind there with entreaties and the like. ॥32॥
2.2.22.33: By the groups dwelling in the city, revered by the mountain king, who seek your noble affection, instruction will indeed always be given you day by day with affection, virtues and the like, even when you are sorrowful. ॥33॥
2.2.22.34: Do you wish to go, beloved, to the mountain surrounded by clusters of bowers, full of varied delights of cuckoos' calls, where spring ever prevails? ॥34॥
2.2.22.35: Do you wish to go to the Himālaya, lord of mountains, with lakes full of many kinds of abundant water, wrapped in coolness, and having lotus ponds by the hundreds? ॥35॥
2.2.22.36: With trees granting all desires, called kalpa trees, and with grassy meadows—see there at leisure the flowers and the herds of horses, elephants and cows. ॥36॥
2.2.22.37: A mountain where the packs of wild beasts are tranquil, thronged by sages and ascetics, an abode of the gods, O Mahāmāyā, filled with herds of many kinds of animals; ॥37॥
2.2.22.38: resplendent with crystal, golden and silver ramparts and the like, and adorned all around with the lovely expanses of lakes such as Mānasa; ॥38॥
2.2.22.39: covered with golden lotuses with jewelled stalks and with buds, and with countless dolphins, tortoises, makaras and other aquatic creatures; ॥39॥
2.2.22.40: frequented by lovely blue lotuses and the like, O Queen of the gods, and by all fragrances and saffron issuing from them. ॥40॥
2.2.22.41: It is adorned by lakes filled with bright, gleaming, fragrant waters of clear radiance, and by fresh, tall grassy meadows lying along the banks. ॥41॥
2.2.22.42: With its śākhoṭa trees that seem to dance, it seems to ward off what is born of itself; it is adorned with amorous sārasa cranes, as with Kāmadevas, and made beautiful by intoxicated cakrāṅga birds. ॥42॥
2.2.22.43: It resounds joyfully with bees and other creatures that hum sweetly and give delight, and it kindles love. ॥43॥
2.2.22.44: Of Indra, of Kubera, of Yama and of Varuṇa, of Agni, of the lord of the south-west quarter, of Vāyu and of the other guardian, ॥44॥
2.2.22.45: — the lofty abode of the gods on Meru, whose peaks are beautified by the cities of these guardians, attended by hosts of fair-thighed women such as Rambhā, Śacī and Menakā. ॥45॥
2.2.22.46: Do you wish to sport on that great mountain, most delightful, which is the very essence of all mountains, the bearers of the earth? ॥46॥
2.2.22.47: There the goddess Śacī, accompanied by her friends and adorned with hosts of Apsarases, will always give you fitting companionship. ॥47॥
2.2.22.48: Or do you wish a place on my Kailāsa, king of mountains, the eternal refuge, resplendent with the city of Kubera, lord of wealth? ॥48॥
2.2.22.49: Kailāsa, purified by the floods of Gaṅgā's waters, with a radiance like the full moon, in whose caves and on whose slopes the daughters of Brahmā ever sing praises, ॥49॥
2.2.22.50: filled with many herds of animals, surrounded by hundreds of lotus-ponds, and in all its qualities more beautiful even than Sumeru with its excellent treasures. ॥50॥
2.2.22.51: Among these places, wherever your heart longs to be, tell me that quickly; I shall make a dwelling for you there. ॥51॥
2.2.22.52: Brahmā said: When Śaṅkara had spoken thus, Dākṣāyaṇī then softly said this to Mahādeva, revealing her own inclination. ॥52॥
2.2.22.53: Satī said: I wish to dwell with you on the Himālaya itself; without delay make our dwelling on that very great mountain. ॥53॥
2.2.22.54: Brahmā said: Then, hearing her words, Hara, utterly enchanted, went with Dākṣāyaṇī to the lofty peak of the Himālaya. ॥54॥
2.2.22.55: He went to a lovely peak, thronged with bands of Siddha women, inaccessible even to birds, and resplendent with lakes and forests. ॥55॥
2.2.22.56: Śambhu, Satī's companion, reached the peak, variegated with jewels and with lotuses of wondrous forms, resembling the rising sun. ॥56॥
2.2.22.57: On that peak, made as of crystal and cloud, resplendent with grassy meadows and trees, furnished with rows of varied flowers and with lakes, ॥57॥
2.2.22.58: a place where the tips of the tree-branches are in full bloom, frequented by humming bees, with blossoming lotuses and clusters of blue water-lilies, ॥58॥
2.2.22.59: adorned with cakravākas and other birds, with kādamba geese, crowded with swans, with intoxicated sārasa cranes, krauñcas, and calling peacocks, ॥59॥
2.2.22.60: with the sweet notes of male cuckoos enjoyed by the hosts, with horse-faced Kinnaras, Siddhas, Apsarases and Guhyakas, ॥60॥
2.2.22.61: a pleasure-ground for Vidyādhara women, goddesses and Kinnara women, and frequented by mountain matrons and maidens, ॥61॥
2.2.22.62: made beautiful by the sounds of vīṇās, stringed instruments, loud mṛdaṅgas and paṭaha drums, and by dancing Apsarases and beings roused by festive delight, ॥62॥
2.2.22.63: well surrounded by fragrant streams and long ponds, and ever adorned with lovely bowers of blossoming flowers — ॥63॥
2.2.22.64: On that peak near the city of the king of mountains, amid such splendours, the bull-bannered Śiva delighted long and beautifully with Satī. ॥64॥
2.2.22.65: In that place equal to heaven, Śaṅkara joyfully sported with Satī for ten thousand years by the measure of the gods. ॥65॥
2.2.22.66: Sometimes Hara would go from that place to another spot; sometimes to the peak of Meru, ever thronged with goddesses and gods. ॥66॥
2.2.22.67: Going again and again to various continents, gardens, forests and the surface of the earth, he would return there once more and enjoy delight with Satī. ॥67॥
2.2.22.68: Day and night he found delight neither in sacrifice, nor in Brahman, nor equally in austerity; Śambhu, with his mind, gave his love to Satī alone. ॥68॥
2.2.22.69: Thus Satī always gazed upon Mahādeva's face, and Mahādeva too, everywhere, ever beheld Satī's face. ॥69॥
2.2.22.70: Thus, through their union with each other, Kālī and Śiva nourished the tree of love by sprinkling it with the waters of their feeling. ॥70॥
2.2.22.iti: Thus ends the twenty-second adhyāya, named The pastimes of Śivā and Śiva, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥22॥
2.2.23.1: Brahmā said: Having thus sported with Śaṅkara, Satī was satisfied, and she became exceedingly dispassionate. ॥1॥
2.2.23.2: One day the goddess Satī, meeting Śiva in private, bowed to him with true devotion, raising her well-formed folded hands high, ॥2॥
2.2.23.3: Having bowed to the very gracious Lord, Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, with folded hands and bent low in humility, then spoke with devotion. ॥3॥
2.2.23.4: Satī said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, ocean of compassion, O Lord, uplifter of the afflicted, great yogin, show mercy upon me. ॥4॥
2.2.23.5: You are the supreme Person, the Master, beyond rajas, sattva and tamas; without attributes and with attributes, the witness, changeless, the great Lord. ॥5॥
2.2.23.6: Blessed am I, who have become your beloved, your loving companion in delightful sport. You have become my husband, O Master, out of your tenderness for devotees, O Hara. ॥6॥
2.2.23.7: For many years, O Lord, supreme sport has been enjoyed by you with me. I am satisfied, O Maheśāna; therefore my mind has turned away from it. ॥7॥
2.2.23.8: I wish to know, O Lord of gods, the supreme truth that brings happiness, by which a living being may easily cross over the sorrow of saṃsāra, O Hara. ॥8॥
2.2.23.9: Doing which even a being attached to sense-objects may attain the supreme state and no longer be bound to saṃsāra, O Lord—tell me that truth; be merciful. ॥9॥
2.2.23.10: Brahmā said: Thus, O sage, Satī—the primal Śakti, the great Goddess—questioned Śaṅkara with true devotion, solely for the uplifting of living beings. ॥10॥
2.2.23.11: Hearing that, Lord Śiva, who assumes a body by his own will, whose mind is detached through yoga, spoke to Satī, supremely pleased. ॥11॥
2.2.23.12: Śiva said: Listen, O goddess, daughter of Dakṣa, great Goddess; I shall declare the supreme truth, by which one bound by latent desires becomes liberated. ॥12॥
2.2.23.13: Know the supreme truth to be realised knowledge (vijñāna), O Parameśvarī, wherein the pure-minded one has no remembrance of a second, knowing, I am Brahman. ॥13॥
2.2.23.14: That is hard to attain in these three worlds; a knower of it is rare, O beloved. Whoever is such is directly Brahman, higher than the highest, and I am his servant. ॥14॥
2.2.23.15: Devotion to me is its mother, granting the fruits of enjoyment and liberation; it is easily attained through my grace and is declared to be ninefold. ॥15॥
2.2.23.16: There is no difference between devotion and knowledge; for the one who practises it there is always happiness. Realised knowledge never arises, O Satī, for one opposed to devotion. ॥16॥
2.2.23.17: Being always subject to devotion, by its power I go even to the houses of the lowly and the casteless, O goddess; there is no doubt. ॥17॥
2.2.23.18: That devotion is held to be twofold, O goddess: with attributes and without attributes. Each is prescribed (vaidhī) or natural (svābhāvikī); the natural is the higher, the other is regarded as lower. ॥18॥
2.2.23.19: By the distinction of steadfast (naiṣṭhikī) and non-steadfast (anaiṣṭhikī), each of those two is again twofold. The steadfast should be known as sixfold; the second is held to be of one kind. ॥19॥
2.2.23.20: By the distinction of enjoined and not enjoined, the wise know it to be manifold; and because these two are of many kinds, their true nature has been described elsewhere. ॥20॥
2.2.23.21: Both of these should be known as having nine limbs, as described by the sages, O beloved. Out of love I shall describe the nine limbs; listen, O daughter of Dakṣa. ॥21॥
2.2.23.22: Listening, singing, remembering, serving, servitude, worship and constant obeisance to me, O goddess, ॥22॥
2.2.23.23: friendship and self-offering—these the wise know as the nine limbs. Its subsidiary limbs, O Śivā, are said to be many. ॥23॥
2.2.23.24: Listen, O goddess, giving your mind to it, to the characteristics of the nine limbs of devotion to me, one by one; they indeed grant enjoyment and liberation. ॥24॥
2.2.23.25: Constantly honouring my stories and the like joyfully with body and the rest, and drinking them in with a steady posture—that is called śravaṇa (listening). ॥25॥
2.2.23.26: Beholding my births and deeds in the space of the heart, and loudly reciting them with love—this is called kīrtana. ॥26॥
2.2.23.27: Seeing me, O goddess, as all-pervading, ever, everywhere and at all times, and being always fearless in the world—that is declared to be smaraṇa. ॥27॥
2.2.23.28: Beginning from dawn, at the time of service, with a reverent heart—and constant fearlessness in the world: that is declared to be smaraṇa. ॥28॥
2.2.23.29: Always serving with all the senses in conformity with the wishes of the one to be served—that indeed is sevana. Service relished as nectar for the heart is declared to be dear dāsya. ॥29॥
2.2.23.30: Always, in the manner of a servant, offering according to rule to me, the Supreme Self, the sixteen services beginning with water for the feet—that is arcana. ॥30॥
2.2.23.31: Touching the ground with the eight limbs while reciting mantra and meditating, with mind and speech in due order—that is called vandana. ॥31॥
2.2.23.32: Whatever auspicious or inauspicious thing my Lord does, all that is for my good: such trust is the mark of sakhya (friendship). ॥32॥
2.2.23.33: Offering everything—body and the rest—for his pleasure, and keeping nothing for one's own maintenance—that is ātmasamarpaṇa (self-surrender). ॥33॥
2.2.23.34: These are the nine limbs of devotion to me; they grant enjoyment and liberation, are exceedingly dear to me, and give rise to knowledge. ॥34॥
2.2.23.35: Many subsidiary limbs of devotion to me are also described, such as worship with bilva leaves and the like; these should be inferred through reflection. ॥35॥
2.2.23.36: Thus devotion to me, with its limbs and sub-limbs, is the highest of all, O beloved; mother of knowledge and dispassion, it shines with liberation as its handmaid. ॥36॥
2.2.23.37: It is the source of the fruits of all actions, ever as dear to me as you; he in whose mind it always abides is ever exceedingly dear to me. ॥37॥
2.2.23.38: In the three worlds there is no path equal to devotion that brings happiness, in all four ages, O Queen of gods—and in Kali especially so. ॥38॥
2.2.23.39: In Kali, knowledge and dispassion, aged in form and joyless, have become utterly decrepit, O goddess, for lack of anyone to take them up. ॥39॥
2.2.23.40: Devotion gives visible fruit in Kali, and in all ages too; by its power I am always under its sway—there is no doubt of this. ॥40॥
2.2.23.41: Whatever man in the world is endowed with devotion, I am always his helper and the remover of his obstacles; his enemy is to be punished by me. There is no doubt about this. ॥41॥
2.2.23.42: For the sake of a devotee, O Goddess, I, overwhelmed with anger, burned Kāla (Death) with the fire born from my eye, as the protector of my own devotee. ॥42॥
2.2.23.43: For the sake of a devotee, O Goddess, I indeed rose up against the Sun long ago; filled with great anger, seizing my trident, I subdued him. ॥43॥
2.2.23.44: For the sake of a devotee, O Goddess, I in anger abandoned Rāvaṇa together with his hosts; I showed him no partiality at all. ॥44॥
2.2.23.45: For the sake of a devotee, O Goddess, I in anger expelled Vyāsa, who had taken up a wrong view, from Kāśī, having had him punished by Nandin. ॥45॥
2.2.23.46: What use is saying much, O Queen of the gods? I am always subject to devotion; I am wholly under the control of the man who practises it. There is no doubt about this. ॥46॥
2.2.23.47: Brahmā said: Having thus heard of the greatness of devotion, Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, rejoiced exceedingly in her mind and joyfully bowed to Śiva. ॥47॥
2.2.23.48: Again, O sage, with true devotion she asked about the subject of that section — the scripture that brings happiness in the world and is devoted to the uplifting of living beings, ॥48॥
2.2.23.49: and the science of mantras together with yantras, and especially its greatness, and other matters of dharma that indeed bring about the uplifting of living beings. ॥49॥
2.2.23.50: Śaṅkara too, hearing Satī's question, his mind delighted, described it all in full with great affection for the uplifting of living beings. ॥50॥
2.2.23.51: Maheśvara expounded the Tantra scripture together with the yantras and with its five limbs, and also the glory of each of the excellent deities. ॥51॥
2.2.23.52: He described the stories of them together with their legendary histories, and the greatness of the devotees, along with the duties of the classes and stages of life, and the duties of kings, O lord of sages; ॥52॥
2.2.23.53: the greatness of the duties of sons and women, the imperishable order of classes and stages of life, the science of medicine, and likewise the science of astronomy, which brings happiness to living beings; ॥53॥
2.2.23.54: the excellent science of bodily marks (sāmudrika) and many other sciences besides — all these the great Lord, showing compassion, described in their true nature. ॥54॥
2.2.23.55: Thus Satī and Śiva, the givers of happiness to the three worlds and all-knowing, who had assumed bodies endowed with good qualities in order to benefit the world, ॥55॥
2.2.23.56: then sported in many ways on Kailāsa, on the Himālaya mountain, and in other places — they whose very nature is the supreme Brahman. ॥56॥
2.2.23.iti: Thus ends the twenty-third adhyāya, named The power of devotion, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥23॥
2.2.24.1: Nārada said: O Brahmā, O Creator, lord of creatures, greatly wise one, mine of compassion: you have let me hear the auspicious glory of Śaṅkara, of Satī and Śaṅkara. ॥1॥
2.2.24.2: Now, out of true affection, tell me that further, most excellent glory: what did the auspicious couple, Śiva and Śivā, do while dwelling there? Tell me their deeds. ॥2॥
2.2.24.3: Brahmā said: Hear from me lovingly, O sage, the story of Satī and Śiva. Adopting the way of the world, they sported always, day after day. ॥3॥
2.2.24.4: Then, O sage, the great goddess Satī suffered separation from her own husband Śaṅkara — so some wise people say. ॥4॥
2.2.24.5: Śakti and Īśa are ever united like word and meaning, and are pure consciousness; how, in truth, could separation between the two occur, O sage? ॥5॥
2.2.24.6: Or else, because of their fondness for play, all that may well fit — whatever the two lords, Satī and Īśa, do while following the ways of worldly existence. ॥6॥
2.2.24.7: Abandoned by her husband, Dakṣa's daughter went to her father's sacrifice, and, seeing there the disrespect shown to Śambhu, she gave up her body. ॥7॥
2.2.24.8: Again, that same Satī was born in the house of Himālaya, Pārvatī by name; having performed abundant austerities, she obtained Śiva through marriage. ॥8॥
2.2.24.9: Sūta said: Having heard these words of Brahmā, Nārada then asked the Creator about the great glory of Śivā and Śiva. ॥9॥
2.2.24.10: Nārada said: O disciple of Viṣṇu, O most fortunate Creator, tell me in detail that story of Śivā and Śiva which closely follows worldly conduct. ॥10॥
2.2.24.11: Why did Śaṅkara abandon his wife, dearer to him than life? Tell me that, dear father, for we consider it strange. ॥11॥
2.2.24.12: O Unborn one, why was there disrespect toward Śiva at the sacrifice of your son? How did she give up her body after going there to her father's sacrifice? ॥12॥
2.2.24.13: What happened there then? What did Maheśvara do? Tell me all that; I am full of faith to hear it. ॥13॥
2.2.24.14: Brahmā said: Listen with great love, dear Nārada, together with the sages, O best of sons, greatly wise one, to the story of the moon-crested Śiva. ॥14॥
2.2.24.15: Having bowed to Maheśāna, the supreme Brahman, served by Hari and the other gods, I shall narrate his most wonderful story. ॥15॥
2.2.24.16: All this is indeed Śiva's play; the Lord is the performer of many sports, independent and changeless; and Satī too is of the same nature. ॥16॥
2.2.24.17: Otherwise, who would be capable of performing those deeds, O sage? He alone is the supreme Self, the supreme Brahman, the Supreme Lord. ॥17॥
2.2.24.18: He whom the Lord of Śrī Viṣṇu always worships, and I too, and all the gods, the great-souled sages, the Siddhas, and Sanaka and the others — ॥18॥
2.2.24.19: — whose glory Śeṣa sings joyfully, constantly, yet never reaches its end, dear one — that Lord is Śaṅkara, Śiva. ॥19॥
2.2.24.20: By his play alone is all this confusion about reality; no one is at fault in it; he, the all-pervading, is the one who impels. ॥20॥
2.2.24.21: Once Rudra Bhava, expert in play, mounted his bull and roamed over the earth in the three worlds together with Satī. ॥21॥
2.2.24.22: Roaming the sea-girdled earth, the Lord, true to his word, came to the Daṇḍaka forest, showing Satī the beauty found there. ॥22॥
2.2.24.23: There Hara saw Rāma, accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, searching for his beloved Sītā, who had been carried off by Rāvaṇa through trickery, ॥23॥
2.2.24.24: crying out, alas, Sītā, his mind overcome by separation, looking here and there, weeping again and again, ॥24॥
2.2.24.25: longing to find her, asking the trees and others in his heart where she had gone, his wits lost, without shame, overwhelmed by grief, ॥25॥
2.2.24.26: the hero born of the Solar dynasty, the king, son of Daśaratha, elder brother of Bharata, bereft of joy and of his radiance. ॥26॥
2.2.24.27: Hara, whose desires are all fulfilled, of noble mind, joyfully bowed to Rāma, who was bound by a boon, as he wandered in the forest with Lakṣmaṇa. ॥27॥
2.2.24.28: Saying, victory to you, Śaṅkara, who is affectionate to his devotees, went elsewhere and did not reveal himself to Rāma in that forest. ॥28॥
2.2.24.29: Seeing such a bewildering play of Śiva, Satī, greatly astonished and deluded by Śiva's māyā, spoke to Śiva. ॥29॥
2.2.24.30: Satī said: O God of gods, supreme Brahman, Lord of all, Supreme Lord, all the gods — Hari, Brahmā and the rest — always serve you. ॥30॥
2.2.24.31: You are to be bowed to by all, to be served and meditated upon at all times; you are knowable through Vedānta with effort, changeless, the supreme Lord. ॥31॥
2.2.24.32: Who are these two men, O Lord, whose appearance is distraught by separation, wandering in the forest, afflicted and wretched — two heroes bearing bows? ॥32॥
2.2.24.33: For what reason, on seeing the elder of the two, dark as a blue lotus, did you just now become delighted and deeply pleased at heart, like a devotee? ॥33॥
2.2.24.34: Please dispel this doubt of mine, O master Śaṅkara: it is not at all fitting, O Lord, that the one who is served should bow to a servant. ॥34॥
2.2.24.35: Brahmā said: The goddess Satī, the primordial Śakti, Śivā, the Supreme Goddess, having come under the sway of Śiva's māyā, questioned the Lord Śiva in this way. ॥35॥
2.2.24.36: Hearing those words of Satī, Śaṅkara, the Supreme Lord, expert in play, then laughed and spoke to Satī. ॥36॥
2.2.24.37: The Supreme Lord said: Listen lovingly, goddess Satī; I speak the truth, not deceit: it was by the power of a boon I had granted that I made the obeisance thus, with respect. ॥37॥
2.2.24.38: They are two brothers named Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, esteemed by heroes, born of the Solar dynasty, O goddess, wise sons of Daśaratha. ॥38॥
2.2.24.39: Of the two of noble complexion, the younger brother, named Lakṣmaṇa, is a portion of Lord Śeṣa; the elder, named Rāma, is Viṣṇu, a full portion, free from all harm. ॥39॥
2.2.24.40: He has descended to earth to protect the good and for our welfare. Having said this, Śambhu, the Lord, the creator, fell silent. ॥40॥
2.2.24.41: Even after hearing such words of Śambhu, her mind did not believe. Śiva's māyā is powerful; it alone deludes the three worlds. ॥41॥
2.2.24.42: Knowing that her mind was unconvinced, the eternal Śambhu, the Lord skilled in divine play, spoke these words. ॥42॥
2.2.24.43: Śiva said: Listen to my words, O Goddess: if your mind does not believe, then go there and test Rāma by your own understanding. ॥43॥
2.2.24.44: Do whatever will make your delusion vanish, O Satī, my beloved. Go there and be the examiner; meanwhile I shall stay at the banyan tree. ॥44॥
2.2.24.45: Brahmā said: By Śiva's command the Goddess Satī went there and reflected: How shall I test Rāma, the forest-wanderer? ॥45॥
2.2.24.46: I shall assume the form of Sītā and go into Rāma's presence. If Rāma is Hari, he will know everything; otherwise not. ॥46॥
2.2.24.47: Having thus reflected, Satī, given over to delusion, became Sītā and went near Rāma in order to test him. ॥47॥
2.2.24.48: Seeing Satī in the form of Sītā, and repeating the name Śiva, the scion of Raghu laughed, recognised the matter, bowed, and spoke. ॥48॥
2.2.24.49: Śrī Rāma said: Salutations to you. Tell me lovingly, O Satī, where has Śambhu gone? Why have you come alone into the forest without your husband? ॥49॥
2.2.24.50: Why have you abandoned your own form and taken on this form, O Satī? Tell me the reason, O Goddess, showing kindness to me. ॥50॥
2.2.24.51: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Rāma, Satī was then astonished; remembering what Śiva had said and realising it was true, she was deeply ashamed. ॥51॥
2.2.24.52: Recognising that Rāma was Viṣṇu, resuming her own form, and remembering Śiva's feet in her heart, Satī, calm in mind, spoke. ॥52॥
2.2.24.53: The Lord Śiva, wandering the earth with me and his attendants, came here into the forest — the independent Supreme Lord. ॥53॥
2.2.24.54: Here he saw you, intent on searching for Sītā, with Lakṣmaṇa, separated from her, your mind afflicted on account of Sītā. ॥54॥
2.2.24.55: Having bowed to you, he went and is staying at the foot of the banyan tree, joyfully praising your supreme Vaiṣṇava greatness. ॥55॥
2.2.24.56: He was not so delighted on seeing you as the four-armed Hari as the bliss he attained on seeing this pure form of yours. ॥56॥
2.2.24.57: Hearing those words of Śambhu, doubt arose in my mind, and by his command I have tested you, O Rāghava. ॥57॥
2.2.24.58: I have come to know, Rāma, that you are Viṣṇu; your entire lordship has been seen, and I am free of doubt. Even so, listen to this, O great-minded one. ॥58॥
2.2.24.59: How is it that you are one to be bowed to by him? Tell me the truth in my presence. Make me free of doubt, and quickly attain full peace. ॥59॥
2.2.24.60: Brahmā said: Hearing her words thus, Rāma, his eyes wide with joy, remembered his own Lord Śambhu, and great love arose in his heart. ॥60॥
2.2.24.61: O sage, without Satī's permission he did not go near Śambhu; and having described Śiva's greatness, Rāghava spoke to Satī. ॥61॥
2.2.24.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fourth adhyāya, named The testing of Rāma, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥24॥
2.2.25.1: Śrī Rāma said: Once, long ago, O goddess, Śambhu, the maker of the supreme creation, summoned Viśvakarman in his own world, which is beyond the highest, ॥1॥
2.2.25.2: and through him had a spacious, delightful mansion properly built in his own cow-pen, and there an excellent throne. ॥2॥
2.2.25.3: There Śaṅkara had Viśvakarman make a supremely divine umbrella, ever wondrous and excellent, for the sake of warding off obstacles. ॥3॥
2.2.25.4: He quickly invited all the hosts of deities headed by Śakra, and the Siddhas, Gandharvas, Nāgas and others, and the demigods in their entirety, ॥4॥
2.2.25.5: all the gods, the Āgamas, the sons of Vidhi (Brahmā) and the sages too, and all the goddesses together with the Apsarases, furnished with various articles. ॥5॥
2.2.25.6: They brought auspicious maidens, sixteen each, of the gods, of the sages, of the Siddhas and of the serpents too. ॥6॥
2.2.25.7: O sage, he had a festival held, having various kinds of instruments, chief among them the vīṇā and mṛdaṅga, played along with fine singers. ॥7॥
2.2.25.8: He had materials fit for a royal consecration, with all the herbs, and five jars filled with the waters of the manifest sacred fords, ॥8॥
2.2.25.9: and likewise other divine requisites he then had brought by his gaṇas; Śaṅkara had a great resounding chant of the Veda performed. ॥9॥
2.2.25.10: Then, having summoned Hari from Vaikuṇṭha, Maheśvara, pleased at heart, rejoiced, O goddess, at his full devotion. ॥10॥
2.2.25.11: At an auspicious moment Mahādeva lovingly seated Hari there on the excellent throne and adorned him completely. ॥11॥
2.2.25.12: Maheśa himself consecrated him, on whom a lovely crown had been fastened and for whom the auspicious thread-rites had been performed, in the pavilion of the cosmic egg. ॥12॥
2.2.25.13: He gave him all the sovereignty that was his own and that goes to no other. Then Śambhu, the independent one, affectionate to devotees, praised him. ॥13॥
2.2.25.14: And he spoke these words to Brahmā, the creator of the worlds, making it known that he, though independent, is subject to the boons he grants, being affectionate to devotees. ॥14॥
2.2.25.15: Maheśa said: From now on, O lord of the world, by my command this Hari, Viṣṇu himself, has become worthy of reverence even by me; let everyone hear this. ॥15॥
2.2.25.16: Dear one, together with all the gods and others, bow to this Hari. Let these Vedas of mine, by my command, describe Hari as they describe me. ॥16॥
2.2.25.17: Śrī Rāma said: Having said this, Rudra himself then bowed to the Garuḍa-bannered one, his heart pleased by Viṣṇu's devotion, the boon-giver affectionate to devotees. ॥17॥
2.2.25.18: Then Hari was saluted by the gods headed by Brahmā, likewise by deities of all forms, and by the sages, Siddhas and others. ॥18॥
2.2.25.19: Then Maheśa, greatly pleased and affectionate to devotees, proclaimed and granted great boons to Hari in front of the celestials. ॥19॥
2.2.25.20: Maheśa said: By my command you are the maker, sustainer and destroyer of all worlds, the giver of dharma, wealth and desire, the chastiser of wrongdoers. ॥20॥
2.2.25.21: You will be lord of the world, worshipped by the world, of great strength and valour, unconquerable anywhere in battle, even by me. ॥21॥
2.2.25.22: Receive the triad of powers beginning with will, conferred by me, the power of various sports, and independence in the three worlds. ॥22॥
2.2.25.23: Those who hate you, O Hari, shall surely be punished by me with effort; to your devotees, O Viṣṇu, the supreme liberation shall be given by me. ॥23॥
2.2.25.24: Receive also this Māyā, hard to repel even for the gods and others, by which the universe, deluded, will become insentient in nature. ॥24॥
2.2.25.25: You are my own arm, and this Vidhi (Brahmā) is the right one, O Hari; of this Vidhi too you will be the protector and also the begetter. ॥25॥
2.2.25.26: Rudra, who is my heart, is I myself, no doubt; he is always to be worshipped by you, and surely by Brahmā and the others too. ॥26॥
2.2.25.27: Abiding here, protect the whole world especially, through various distinct incarnations and always with various agents of protection. ॥27॥
2.2.25.28: In my world this abode of yours, of supreme prosperity and greatly radiant, will be renowned as Goloka. ॥28॥
2.2.25.29: Those incarnations of yours, O Hari, which will be protectors on earth and devoted to me, I shall surely behold, pleased by my own boon. ॥29॥
2.2.25.30: Śrī Rāma said: Having thus brought about Hari's undivided sovereignty, Hara himself, Umā's lord, sports freely on Kailāsa with his gaṇas. ॥30॥
2.2.25.31: From that time the lord of Lakṣmī took on a cowherd's guise, and went there with great delight, the lord of cowherds, cowherd women and cows. ॥31॥
2.2.25.32: That Viṣṇu too, pleased in spirit, protected the whole world, assuming various incarnations and carrying out its protection by Śiva's command. ॥32॥
2.2.25.33: Now, by Śaṅkara's command, he has descended here in fourfold form: I, Rāma, and Bharata, Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna. ॥33॥
2.2.25.34: Then, O goddess Satī, by my father's command I came to the forest with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, and today I have become distressed through fate. ॥34॥
2.2.25.35: My wife, Sītā, has been carried off by some night-wanderer; separated from her, I am searching here in the forest for my beloved with my brother. ॥35॥
2.2.25.36: Since I have obtained your sight, all will surely be well with me, no doubt, O mother Satī, by your grace. ॥36॥
2.2.25.37: The boon of recovering Sītā will come about, O goddess, no doubt, once I slay that sinful, sorrow-causing demon, by your favour. ॥37॥
2.2.25.38: Great is my fortune this very day, since you two have shown me compassion. The man toward whom you two are compassionate is blessed and excellent. ॥38॥
2.2.25.39: Having spoken thus in many ways and bowed deeply to Satī, Śivā, the scion of Raghu, at her bidding, wandered in that forest. ॥39॥
2.2.25.40: Then, having heard the words of the self-controlled Rāma, Satī became delighted in her heart with him, who was praising Śiva and devoted to Śiva-bhakti. ॥40॥
2.2.25.41: Remembering her own deed, she grieved deeply in her mind. Dejected and pale, she returned to Śiva's presence. ॥41॥
2.2.25.42: As she walked on the way, the goddess thought again and again: I did not accept what Śiva said; I formed a wrong notion about Rāma. ॥42॥
2.2.25.43: What answer shall I give when I go before Śaṅkara? Thinking this over in many ways, she was then seized by remorse. ॥43॥
2.2.25.44: Having gone near Śambhu, she bowed to Śiva in her heart, her face downcast, distraught with grief, her radiance gone. ॥44॥
2.2.25.45: Then Hara, seeing her distressed, asked after her welfare and said kindly: How was the test of him carried out? ॥45॥
2.2.25.46: Hearing Śiva's words, she said nothing at all; with her face bowed, Satī, stricken with grief, stood there close by. ॥46॥
2.2.25.47: Then Maheśa, the great yogin skilled in manifold sports, meditated and understood in his heart what Dakṣa's daughter had done. ॥47॥
2.2.25.48: He remembered his own vow, made earlier because of Hari's indignation; then that Rudra, the upholder of propriety, was as if entreated by him to keep it. ॥48॥
2.2.25.49: Sorrow came over the Lord there, and he spoke thus in his mind—he who is ever the speaker of dharma, the doer of dharma, and the protector of dharma. ॥49॥
2.2.25.50: Śiva said: If I were to show love to Dakṣa's daughter as great as before, my pure vow would be destroyed—mine, who follow the ways of the world in my sport. ॥50॥
2.2.25.51: Brahmā said: Having reflected thus in many ways, he abandoned Satī in his heart; the protector of Vedic dharma did not break his vow. ॥51॥
2.2.25.52: Then the Supreme Lord, having renounced Satī in his mind, went to his own mountain; that Lord indeed plainly expressed the separation. ॥52॥
2.2.25.53: As Maheśvara moved along the way, a voice from the sky spoke to him, making all there hear it, and Dakṣa's daughter in particular. ॥53॥
2.2.25.54: The heavenly voice said: Blessed are you, O Supreme Lord, and so too is such a vow! Today there is no one else equal to you in these three worlds, O great yogin, great Lord. ॥54॥
2.2.25.55: Brahmā said: Hearing the voice from the sky, the goddess, her radiance faded, asked Śiva: What vow have you made, Lord? Tell me, O Supreme Lord. ॥55॥
2.2.25.56: Though asked thus, Giriśa, the Lord who sought Satī's welfare, did not disclose to her his vow, which he had made long before in Hari's presence. ॥56॥
2.2.25.57: Then Satī, meditating on Śiva, her husband, dear as her life, understood the whole cause—that it amounted to abandonment by her beloved, O sage. ॥57॥
2.2.25.58: Then, having realised that she had been abandoned by Śambhu, Dakṣa's daughter at once grieved exceedingly, sighing again and again. ॥58॥
2.2.25.59: Śiva, perceiving her state, kept hidden his inner feeling and his own vow from Satī, the Lord telling her many stories. ॥59॥
2.2.25.60: Telling various stories, he reached Kailāsa with Satī. Seated in an excellent place, the yogin assumed his own form and entered into samādhi. ॥60॥
2.2.25.61: Satī stayed there in that abode, her mind greatly troubled. No one knew of that affair between Śiva and Satī, O sage. ॥61॥
2.2.25.62: Thus a long time passed for the two of them, O great sage—the two Lords who had taken bodies of their own accord and were following the play of the world. ॥62॥
2.2.25.63: Then Giriśa, the bestower of supreme protection, gave up his meditation. Knowing this, Satī, the Mother of the world, came there. ॥63॥
2.2.25.64: Then the goddess bowed to Śiva with an aching heart. Magnanimous Śambhu gave her a seat facing him. ॥64॥
2.2.25.65: With great affection he told her many charming stories, and by such sport he at once freed her from grief. ॥65॥
2.2.25.66: She attained happiness as before, yet he did not give up his vow. This should not be thought astonishing in Śiva, the Supreme Lord, dear child. ॥66॥
2.2.25.67: Thus do sages tell the story of Śivā and Śiva, O sage. Some, being ignorant, speak of a separation—but how could there be separation between those two? ॥67॥
2.2.25.68: Who truly knows the doings of Śivā and Śiva? Sporting at their own will, the two ever enact their deeds. ॥68॥
2.2.25.69: Satī and Śiva are ever united like word and meaning. Separation between them is inconceivable; it could occur only by their own will. ॥69॥
2.2.25.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fifth adhyāya, named The separation of Satī, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥25॥
2.2.26.1: Brahmā said: Long ago there took place, performed according to rule, a great sacrifice of all the great-souled sages who had assembled at Prayāga. ॥1॥
2.2.26.2: There came the Siddhas, the divine sages headed by Sanaka, and the gods together with the Prajāpatis, men of wisdom who had seen Brahman. ॥2॥
2.2.26.3: I too came there with my retinue, accompanied by the Nigamas and Āgamas in embodied form, of great splendour. ॥3॥
2.2.26.4: Their assembly was indeed wonderful and full of festivity; there arose discussion of knowledge drawn from many scriptures. ॥4॥
2.2.26.5: At that moment, O sage, the Lord Rudra, with Bhavānī and his Gaṇas, the master who brings about the welfare of the three worlds and is the cause of creation, came there. ॥5॥
2.2.26.6: Seeing Śiva, all the gods, the Siddhas and the sages bowed to that Lord with devotion and praised him, and so did I. ॥6॥
2.2.26.7: At Śiva's command all took their proper places, filled with joy, delighted at the sight of the Lord and extolling their own good fortune. ॥7॥
2.2.26.8: At that moment Dakṣa, the lord of the Prajāpatis, powerful, very pleased and radiant, arrived there by chance. ॥8॥
2.2.26.9: Having bowed to me, that Dakṣa sat down there at my bidding—the respected ruler of the cosmic egg, proud, and averse to the truth. ॥9॥
2.2.26.10: Dakṣa, of excellent splendour, was honoured with praises and prostrations by all the divine sages, who humbly joined their palms. ॥10॥
2.2.26.11: But Maheśvara, the Lord who sports in many ways, independent, the supreme protector, seated on his own seat, did not then bow to Dakṣa. ॥11॥
2.2.26.12: Seeing Hara there not bowing, that son of mine, Dakṣa the Prajāpati, his mind displeased, suddenly became angry with Rudra. ॥12॥
2.2.26.13: Looking at Rudra, the great Lord, with a cruel glance, the very arrogant one, devoid of wisdom, spoke loudly so that all could hear. ॥13॥
2.2.26.14: Dakṣa said: All these gods and demons, the best of brāhmaṇas and the sages bow deeply to me. How then has this great-minded one, who is surrounded by ghosts and goblins, behaved like a wicked man? ॥14॥
2.2.26.15: This shameless dweller in cremation grounds—how does he not now bow to me? He has abandoned rites, is served by spirits and goblins, is mad, lawless, and always a defiler of right conduct. ॥15॥
2.2.26.16: Heretics, wicked and sinful by nature, become arrogant and abusive on seeing a brāhmaṇa; and he is ever attached to his wife, skilled in love-play. Therefore I am set to curse him. ॥16॥
2.2.26.17: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, that great villain, filled with fury, then said this to Rudra: Let these best of brāhmaṇas and gods listen; you ought to make him one fit to be punished by me. ॥17॥
2.2.26.18: Dakṣa said: This Rudra is excluded by me from the sacrifice; he is beyond the classes and of degraded form. Let him not receive a share together with the gods—this dweller in cremation grounds, devoid of family and birth. ॥18॥
2.2.26.19: Brahmā said: Hearing what Dakṣa said, Bhṛgu and many others reviled Rudra, regarding him as a wicked being, merely on a par with the gods. ॥19॥
2.2.26.20: Hearing those words, Nandī the Gaṇa, his eyes rolling, extremely enraged and intent on giving a curse, quickly spoke to Dakṣa. ॥20॥
2.2.26.21: Nandīśvara said: O you rogue, great fool, Dakṣa of wicked mind, how have you made my master Maheśa excluded from the sacrifice? ॥21॥
2.2.26.22: By the mere remembrance of whom sacrifices become fruitful and holy places become pure—how has this Hara been cursed? ॥22॥
2.2.26.23: In vain, O evil-minded Dakṣa, out of brāhmaṇical rashness, have you cursed him; in vain too has the faultless Rudra, the great Lord, been ridiculed. ॥23॥
2.2.26.24: By whom this universe is created, protected and at the end destroyed—how has that Rudra, Maheśa, been cursed, O vilest of brāhmaṇas? ॥24॥
2.2.26.25: Thus rebuked by Nandī, the Prajāpati Dakṣa, filled with rage, then cursed Nandī. ॥25॥
2.2.26.26: Dakṣa said: May all of you Gaṇas of Rudra be outside the Vedas, cut off from the Vedic path, and likewise abandoned by the great sages. ॥26॥
2.2.26.27: May you be devoted to heretical doctrines, excluded from the conduct of the cultured, addicted to drinking liquor, wearing matted locks, ashes and bones. ॥27॥
2.2.26.28: Brahmā said: When Śiva's servants had been thus cursed by Dakṣa, Nandī, dear to Śiva, hearing it, became possessed by intense fury. ॥28॥
2.2.26.29: Nandī, the son of Śilāda, radiant and beloved of Śiva, quickly replied to that arrogant great villain Dakṣa. ॥29॥
2.2.26.30: Nandīśvara said: O Dakṣa, rogue, evil-minded one, utterly in vain have Śiva's servants been cursed by you, out of brāhmaṇical rashness, not knowing the truth of Śiva. ॥30॥
2.2.26.31: O egotist, the great Lord Maheśāna has been mocked by the wicked-minded fools Bhṛgu and the rest, out of their brāhmaṇical pride. ॥31॥
2.2.26.32: Upon those brāhmaṇas here who are hostile to Rudra, villains like you, I pronounce a curse by virtue of the power of Rudra's might. ॥32॥
2.2.26.33: May you brāhmaṇas be forever attached to the mere words of the Veda, turned away from the true essence of the Veda, declaring that there is nothing else. ॥33॥
2.2.26.34: May the brāhmaṇas forever be full of desires, intent on heaven, possessed by anger, greed and pride, shameless beggars. ॥34॥
2.2.26.35: Putting forward the Vedic path as a pretext, the brāhmaṇas will officiate at sacrifices for śūdras; they will be poor, ever eager to receive gifts. ॥35॥
2.2.26.36: Accepting gifts from the unworthy, all of them will go to hell, O Dakṣa, and some will become brahmarākṣasas. ॥36॥
2.2.26.37: This evil-minded fool who, regarding Śiva, the Supreme Lord, as an ordinary god, bears him hatred—may he be turned away from the truth. ॥37॥
2.2.26.38: May he, out of desire for vulgar pleasures, ever propagate in households of false dharma the system of rituals and the mere Vedic talk, perpetually. ॥38॥
2.2.26.39: May Dakṣa, his face bereft of joy, a beast who has forgotten the goal of the Self, delighting in fallen rites and wrong conduct, soon become goat-faced. ॥39॥
2.2.26.40: When the brāhmaṇas had been cursed there by the angry Nandī, and the Lord had been cursed by Dakṣa, a great cry of dismay arose. ॥40॥
2.2.26.41: Hearing that, I, the creator of the Vedas and knower of Śiva's true nature, reproached him severely again and again, and also the brahmins Bhṛgu and the others. ॥41॥
2.2.26.42: The Lord Sadāśiva too, hearing Nandin's words, spoke sweet words as if smiling, instructing him. ॥42॥
2.2.26.43: Sadāśiva said: Listen, O Nandin, greatly wise one: you ought not to become angry. Thinking by mistake that I had been cursed, you have cursed the brahmin race in vain. ॥43॥
2.2.26.44: The Veda is made of mantra-syllables and is wholly composed of hymns; and in the hymn is established the self of all embodied beings. ॥44॥
2.2.26.45: Therefore you should never, filled with anger, curse the knowers of the self. The Vedas are never to be cursed by anyone, not even by one of evil mind. ॥45॥
2.2.26.46: And I have not been cursed now — you should understand this in truth. Be calm, O greatly intelligent one, you who are the instructor of Sanaka and the others. ॥46॥
2.2.26.47: I am the sacrifice, I am the sacrificial rite, and all the limbs of the sacrifice entirely; I alone am the soul of the sacrifice, the one devoted to sacrifice, and the one beyond the sacrifice. ॥47॥
2.2.26.48: Who is this one, who are you, who indeed are these? In truth, I am everything. Reflect on this with your intellect; the brahmins were cursed by you in vain. ॥48॥
2.2.26.49: Having dispelled the construction of the phenomenal world through knowledge of the truth, be wise and self-abiding, O great-minded Nandin, free from anger and the like. ॥49॥
2.2.26.50: Brahmā said: Thus enlightened by Śambhu, Nandikeśvara became supremely discerning and grew calm, free from anger. ॥50॥
2.2.26.51: Śiva too, having quickly enlightened his own gaṇa, dear to him as life, went joyfully with his gaṇas from there to his own abode. ॥51॥
2.2.26.52: Dakṣa too, possessed by anger and surrounded by those brahmins, went to his own place, his mind intent on hostility toward Śiva. ॥52॥
2.2.26.53: Then, remembering Rudra as he had been cursing him, Dakṣa, filled with intense anger and deluded in mind, cast off all faith and became intent on reviling the worshippers of Śiva. ॥53॥
2.2.26.54: Evil-minded Dakṣa, though thus addressed by Śambhu, the Supreme Self — listen, dear child, I shall tell you of his extreme wickedness of mind. ॥54॥
2.2.26.iti: Thus ends the twenty-sixth adhyāya, named Dakṣa's enmity with Śiva, in the account of Satī, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥26॥
2.2.27.1: Brahmā said: Once, O sage, a great sacrifice was begun by him Dakṣa. Then all the divine sages were invited there by him, the consecrated one. ॥1॥
2.2.27.2: All the great sages and the gods assembled there for the performance of that sacrifice, deluded by Śiva's māyā. ॥2॥
2.2.27.3: Agastya, Kaśyapa, Atri, Vāmadeva and Bhṛgu, Dadhīci, the blessed Vyāsa, Bhāradvāja and Gautama, ॥3॥
2.2.27.4: Paila, Parāśara, Garga, Bhārgava, Kakubha, Sita, Sumantu, Trika and Kaṅka, and Vaiśampāyana too — ॥4॥
2.2.27.5: these and many other sages went joyfully, with their wives and sons, to the sacrifice of my son Dakṣa. ॥5॥
2.2.27.6: Likewise all the hosts of gods, the illustrious guardians of the worlds, and likewise all the minor deities, furnished with their own equipment and forces came. ॥6॥
2.2.27.7: I, the maker of the universe, having been praised, was brought from Satyaloka, with my sons and retinue, accompanied by the embodied Vedas and the rest. ॥7॥
2.2.27.8: Likewise Viṣṇu, having been entreated with manifold respect, was brought from Vaikuṇṭha to the sacrifice together with his attendants and retinue. ॥8॥
2.2.27.9: In this way others too, deluded, came to Dakṣa's sacrifice, and all of them were honoured by that evil-minded Dakṣa. ॥9॥
2.2.27.10: Very costly, brilliant, spacious and divine mansions, built by Tvaṣṭṛ, were given to them by him. ॥10॥
2.2.27.11: Lodged in all those abodes according to their rank, and duly honoured, they all shone, together with Viṣṇu and me. ॥11॥
2.2.27.12: Then, as the great sacrifice was proceeding at the sacred ford of Kanakhala, Bhṛgu and other ascetics rich in penance were appointed by him as officiating priests. ॥12॥
2.2.27.13: Viṣṇu himself, with all the hosts of Maruts, was the presiding authority; and I, Brahmā, was there as the expounder of the rules of the three Vedas. ॥13॥
2.2.27.14: Likewise all the guardians of the quarters were gatekeepers and protectors, armed and with their retinues, ever eager in their duty. ॥14॥
2.2.27.15: Yajña himself, in a beautiful form, attended his sacrifice, and all the foremost great sages became themselves the bearers of the Vedas. ॥15॥
2.2.27.16: Fire (Tanūnapāt) too made his own form thousandfold, to receive the oblations swiftly at that sacrifice, a great festival. ॥16॥
2.2.27.17: Eighty-eight thousand priests offered oblations together; the udgātṛ priests, divine sages, numbered sixty-four thousand. ॥17॥
2.2.27.18: Then there were as many adhvaryu and hotṛ priests, Nārada and others; the seven sages each separately recited uniform hymns (gāthās). ॥18॥
2.2.27.19: Dakṣa chose for his own great sacrifice the hosts of Gandharvas, Vidyādharas and Siddhas, the hosts of Ādityas with their attendants and sacrificial requisites, and all the numerous Nāgas and roaming beings. ॥19॥
2.2.27.20: The hosts of brahmin sages, royal sages and divine sages, kings with their friends, ministers and armies, the Vasus at the head, and the group-deities — all were chosen by him, the director of the sacrifice. ॥20॥
2.2.27.21: Then Dakṣa, consecrated for the rite, having performed the auspicious thread-ceremony and the rites for well-being, shone greatly together with his wife. ॥21॥
2.2.27.22: At that sacrifice Śambhu was not invited by the evil-minded Dakṣa, who concluded: He is a skull-bearer; he is not worthy of the sacrifice. ॥22॥
2.2.27.23: Satī too, his beloved own daughter, was not invited to the sacrifice by Dakṣa, who saw only faults, because she was the skull-bearer's wife. ॥23॥
2.2.27.24: While Dakṣa's sacrifice, a great festival, was thus proceeding, all those approved for the rite were engaged there in their own duties. ॥24॥
2.2.27.25: Meanwhile, not seeing Lord Śaṅkara there, the Śaiva Dadhīca, deeply troubled in mind, spoke these words. ॥25॥
2.2.27.26: Dadhīca said: All of you, headed by the gods and sages, listen gladly to my words: why has Śambhu not come to this sacrifice, this great festival? ॥26॥
2.2.27.27: These lords of the gods and most eminent sages, along with the guardians of the worlds, have assembled; yet the sacrifice does not truly shine without that great-souled Pināka-bearer. ॥27॥
2.2.27.28: He through whom alone all auspicious things come to be, as the great wise ones declare — that ancient Person, bull-bannered, blue-throated, the supreme Lord, is not seen here. ॥28॥
2.2.27.29: O Dakṣa, by whom even inauspicious things, when taken up, become auspicious; and through whom, even in a span of three or five moments, auspicious things at once become supreme beyond the supreme. ॥29॥
2.2.27.30: Therefore the invitation of the supreme Lord must be made quickly by you yourself, or else by Brahmā, or by Viṣṇu, the all-pervading Lord, ॥30॥
2.2.27.31: together now with Indra, the guardians of the worlds, the twice-born and the Siddhas: by all means that Śaṅkara must be brought, for the fulfilment of the sacrifice. ॥31॥
2.2.27.32: All of you should go to where the god Maheśvara is; make haste and bring Śambhu together with Dākṣāyaṇī. ॥32॥
2.2.27.33: O lords of the gods, through that Śambhu, the Supreme Self, coming here with Ambā, everything will become pure. ॥33॥
2.2.27.34: By remembering him and uttering his name, all merit is complete; therefore the bull-bannered one must be brought with every effort. ॥34॥
2.2.27.35: When Śaṅkara has come here, the sacrifice will indeed be purifying; otherwise it will remain incomplete. I speak this truth. ॥35॥
2.2.27.36: Brahmā said: Hearing his words, Dakṣa, filled with anger, foolish and wicked-minded, replied at once, as if laughing. ॥36॥
2.2.27.37: Viṣṇu, the root of the gods, in whom eternal dharma resides, has been duly brought by me. What is lacking in the sacrificial rite? ॥37॥
2.2.27.38: He in whom the Vedas, the sacrifices and the various rites are all established — that Viṣṇu has come here. ॥38॥
2.2.27.39: Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, has come from Satyaloka, together with the Vedas, the Upaniṣads and the various Āgamas. ॥39॥
2.2.27.40: Likewise the king of the gods himself has come with the hosts of gods; and likewise you sages, free from sin, have come. ॥40॥
2.2.27.41: All of you who have assembled here, who are fit for the sacrifice, peaceful, worthy recipients, knowers of the truth of the Vedas and their meaning, are firm in your vows. ॥41॥
2.2.27.42: And here, what need have we even of Rudra? O brahmin, my daughter was given to him by me only because I was urged by Brahmā. ॥42॥
2.2.27.43: O brahmin, that Hara is of no lineage, devoid of father and mother, the sole lord of ghosts, spirits and goblins, hard to deal with. ॥43॥
2.2.27.44: He is self-conceited, foolish, obstinate, silent, and envious. He is not fit for this rite; therefore he has not been invited by me now. ॥44॥
2.2.27.45: Therefore such words must never again be spoken by you anywhere. All of you should make my great sacrifice fruitful. ॥45॥
2.2.27.46: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of his, Dadhīci spoke words full of substance, while all the gods and sages listened. ॥46॥
2.2.27.47: Dadhīca said: Without that Śiva, this has become a great non-sacrifice; indeed, destruction will especially befall you here. ॥47॥
2.2.27.48: Having said this, Dadhīca went out alone from Dakṣa's sacrificial enclosure and quickly went to his own hermitage. ॥48॥
2.2.27.49: Then the other devotees of Śaṅkara, the chief followers of Śiva's doctrine, likewise pronounced a curse and at once departed to their own hermitages. ॥49॥
2.2.27.50: When that sage and the others had gone out from the sacrifice, the evil-minded Dakṣa, hater of Śiva, laughing, said this to the sages. ॥50॥
2.2.27.51: Dakṣa said: The brahmin dear to Śiva, named Dadhīca, has gone; and the others of his kind have also gone from my sacrifice. ॥51॥
2.2.27.52: This has turned out most auspicious and is wholly agreeable to me. I speak the truth, O lord of gods, and you gods and sages as well. ॥52॥
2.2.27.53: Those of ruined minds, dull, devoted to false doctrine, wicked, outside the Veda and of bad conduct, are to be excluded from the sacrificial rite. ॥53॥
2.2.27.54: All of you, headed by Viṣṇu, are devoted to Vedic teaching. O brahmins and gods, make my sacrifice fruitful without delay. ॥54॥
2.2.27.55: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of his, all the gods and sages, deluded by Śiva's māyā, performed the worship of the gods in that sacrifice. ॥55॥
2.2.27.56: Thus the curse on that sacrifice has been described by me, O lord of sages. Now the account of the sacrifice's destruction is being told; listen attentively. ॥56॥
2.2.27.iti: Thus ends the twenty-seventh adhyāya, named The beginning of the sacrifice, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥27॥
2.2.28.1: Brahmā said: When the gods and sages went with festivity to Dakṣa's sacrifice, at that very time the goddess, on Mount Gandhamādana, ॥1॥
2.2.28.2: in a fountain-house with a canopy, surrounded by her friends, Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, engaged in many kinds of grand play. ॥2॥
2.2.28.3: Then the goddess Satī, absorbed in play, joyfully saw the Moon, having taken leave, hastening with Rohiṇī toward Dakṣa's sacrifice. ॥3॥
2.2.28.4: Having seen this, Satī spoke to Vijayā, who was close at her side—her own foremost friend, dear to her as life, and ever bringing her good. ॥4॥
2.2.28.5: Satī said: O best of friends, O Vijayā, dear to me as life, where is this Moon going with Rohiṇī? Ask quickly. ॥5॥
2.2.28.6: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by Satī, Vijayā went quickly into his presence and fittingly asked the Moon, where are you going? ॥6॥
2.2.28.7: Then, having heard what Vijayā said, he respectfully told her first of his own journey—all about Dakṣa's sacrificial festival and the rest. ॥7॥
2.2.28.8: Hearing that, Vijayā, hurried and agitated, told the goddess Satī all that the Moon had said. ॥8॥
2.2.28.9: Hearing that, the goddess Kālikā Satī was then astonished; reflecting, and not finding the reason for it, she pondered in her mind: ॥9॥
2.2.28.10: Dakṣa is my father and Vīriṇī my mother; why have they not invited us two? Have they forgotten me, their beloved daughter? So thought Satī. ॥10॥
2.2.28.11: I shall respectfully ask Śaṅkara the whole reason for this. Having thought thus, she became firmly resolved to go there. ॥11॥
2.2.28.12: Then the goddess Dākṣāyaṇī, leaving her foremost friend Vijayā there, quickly went to Śiva's presence. ॥12॥
2.2.28.13: She saw him seated in the midst of the assembly with many gaṇas—Nandin and other great heroes, the foremost leaders of troops. ॥13॥
2.2.28.14: Having seen him, the Lord Īśāna, her own husband, Dakṣa's daughter then quickly approached Śaṅkara to ask the reason for that. ॥14॥
2.2.28.15: Śiva, full of affection, placed his beloved on his lap and delighted her with words, showing her great honour. ॥15॥
2.2.28.16: Then Śambhu, of great sport, lord of all, giver of happiness to the good, seated amid the gaṇas, quickly and respectfully spoke to Satī. ॥16॥
2.2.28.17: Śambhu said: Why have you come here into the midst of the assembly, looking astonished? Tell me the reason quickly and gladly, O slender-waisted one. ॥17॥
2.2.28.18: Brahmā said: Thus addressed then by Maheśa, O lord of sages, Satī—Śivā—with folded hands, bowing deeply at once, spoke to the Lord. ॥18॥
2.2.28.19: Satī said: I have heard that a great sacrifice of my father is taking place. There is a great festival there; the gods and sages have assembled. ॥19॥
2.2.28.20: Why does going to my father's great sacrifice not please you, O Lord of the god of gods? Tell me all of it, O master. ॥20॥
2.2.28.21: This indeed is the way of kinsfolk: friends keep company with friends, O Mahādeva, which increases affection. ॥21॥
2.2.28.22: Therefore, with every effort, go with me today, O Lord, to my father's sacrificial ground, O master, at my request. ॥22॥
2.2.28.23: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of Satī, the god Maheśvara, his heart pierced by the arrows of Dakṣa's words, spoke kind words. ॥23॥
2.2.28.24: Maheśvara said: Dakṣa, your father, O goddess, is especially hostile to me. ॥24॥
2.2.28.25: All those who honour him—the others, headed by the gods and sages—who have gone to your father's sacrifice are fools, devoid of wisdom. ॥25॥
2.2.28.26: And those who go uninvited to another's house, O goddess, meet with dishonour worse than death. ॥26॥
2.2.28.27: Even Indra, going in that way to another's house, becomes belittled; what then to speak of others? Such a journey is indeed disgraceful. ॥27॥
2.2.28.28: Therefore neither you nor I should by any means go to Dakṣa's sacrifice; I have told you the truth, my dear. ॥28॥
2.2.28.29: A man is not so pained even when wounded by enemies' arrows as he is when struck in his vitals by the harsh words of his own people. ॥29॥
2.2.28.30: When their discernment is destroyed by the six qualities—learning and the rest—which in the good are virtues but in the wicked are otherwise, the wicked do not see the glory of the great, my dear. ॥30॥
2.2.28.31: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by the great-souled Maheśa, Satī, filled with anger, spoke to Śiva, the best of those skilled in speech. ॥31॥
2.2.28.32: Satī said: You, O Śambhu, Lord of all, by whom a sacrifice becomes fruitful—you have not been invited today by that evil-doing father of mine. ॥32॥
2.2.28.33: I wish to know all that, O Bhava—the intention of that wicked one, and of all the wicked gods and sages who have come there. ॥33॥
2.2.28.34: Therefore I am going this very day to my father's sacrifice, O Lord. Give me permission to go there, O master, Maheśvara. ॥34॥
2.2.28.35: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by that goddess, the blessed Rudra, Śiva himself—the seer whose vision knows all, the cause of creation—spoke to Satī. ॥35॥
2.2.28.36: Śiva said: If such is your desire, O goddess, that you must go there, then, O you of good vows, go quickly to your father's sacrifice with my consent. ॥36॥
2.2.28.37: Mount this bull Nandin, made ready with care, and, furnished with great royal honours, endowed with many excellences, go. ॥37॥
2.2.28.38: Told by Rudra to mount the adorned bull, Satī, finely adorned and fully equipped, went to her father's house. ॥38॥
2.2.28.39: Great royal insignia were given to her by the Supreme Self—a fine umbrella, chowries and the like, and excellent garments and ornaments. ॥39॥
2.2.28.40: Sixty thousand fierce gaṇas of Rudra went by Śiva's command, full of curiosity, delighted, and in high festive spirit. ॥40॥
2.2.28.41: Then a great festivity arose there on all sides during the journey of Satī, Śiva's beloved, made by the gaṇas of Vāmadeva. ॥41॥
2.2.28.42: The gaṇas made merriment and sang aloud the glory of Śiva and Śivā; those great heroes, dear to Śiva, leapt about vigourously out of joy. ॥42॥
2.2.28.43: In every way there was great splendour at the departure of the Mother of the world; a joyful clamour arose, and the three worlds were filled with it. ॥43॥
2.2.28.iti: Thus ends the twenty-eighth adhyāya, named Satī's journey, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥28॥
2.2.29.1: Brahmā said: Dākṣāyaṇī went there, where the greatly splendid sacrifice was being held, full of the excitement of gods, asuras, chief sages and others. ॥1॥
2.2.29.2: There she saw her father's mansion, full of many wonders, very splendid and lovely, crowded with hosts of gods and sages. ॥2॥
2.2.29.3: Then the goddess, standing at the gate, dismounted from her own seat, Nandin, and quickly went inside, alone, into the sacrifice. ॥3॥
