2.2.39.17: Seeing that discus with its edge blunted, Dadhīca smilingly spoke to Viṣṇu, the very cause of the manifestation of the existent and the non-existent. ॥17॥
2.2.39.18: Dadhīca said: O Lord, the extremely terrible discus famed as Sudarśana, which you, Viṣṇu, obtained long ago through great effort — that auspicious discus of Bhava does not wish to slay me here. ॥18॥
2.2.39.19: So now, Lord Hari, in your anger discharge all your weapons at me one after another; you should make the effort with arrows and missiles beginning with the Brahmāstra. ॥19॥
2.2.39.20: Brahmā said: Hearing his words and seeing him as a man without might, Hari then in anger discharged all his weapons at him one after another. ॥20॥
2.2.39.21: Then the gods, bereft of understanding, eagerly gave help to Viṣṇu, who had set out to fight a single brahmin. ॥21॥
2.2.39.22: Indra and the others on Hari's side swiftly hurled their own weapons and missiles with force from all sides upon Dadhīca. ॥22॥
2.2.39.23: Then Dadhīca, the self-controlled one with adamantine bones, taking a handful of kuśa grass and remembering Śiva, cast it on all sides at all the gods. ॥23॥
2.2.39.24: By the power of Śaṅkara, that handful of kuśa of the sage became a divine trident resembling the fire of universal destruction, O sage. ॥24॥
2.2.39.25: That Śaiva trident with its prongs, blazing on all sides with splendour surpassing the fire at the end of the age, set its mind on burning the gods along with their weapons. ॥25॥
2.2.39.26: And all the weapons that had been hurled by the gods headed by Nārāyaṇa and Indra bowed down to that three-pronged trident. ॥26॥
2.2.39.27: All the gods, the dwellers of heaven, their valour shattered, fled. Only Hari, the best of illusionists, remained there, frightened. ॥27॥
2.2.39.28: Lord Viṣṇu, the supreme person, created from his own body divine attendants resembling himself, in hundreds of thousands upon tens of thousands. ॥28॥
2.2.39.29: Then those heroic attendants of Viṣṇu also fought there with the lone sage Dadhīca, whose self was Śiva, O divine sage. ॥29॥
2.2.39.30: Then Dadhīca, best of Śaivas, having fought those attendants of Viṣṇu repeatedly in battle, suddenly burnt them all. ॥30॥
2.2.39.31: Then, to astonish the sage Dadhīca, Hari, expert in great illusion, quickly assumed the cosmic form. ॥31॥
2.2.39.32: In that very body of Hari, Dadhīca, best of brahmins, saw thousands of gods and other living beings, ॥32॥
2.2.39.33: and crores of beings, crores of attendants, and crores of cosmic eggs, then, in the body of the cosmic-formed one. ॥33॥
2.2.39.34: Having seen all this there, the son of Cyavana then spoke to Viṣṇu, the lord of the world, praised by the world, the unborn, the all-pervading. ॥34॥
2.2.39.35: Dadhīca said: Give up this illusion, O mighty-armed one; on reflection it is mere appearance. Thousands of things hard to know are known to me, O Mādhava. ॥35॥
2.2.39.36: Look attentively in me at the whole universe together with yourself, and also Brahmā and Rudra; I give you divine sight. ॥36॥
2.2.39.37: Brahmā said: Having said this, the sage, the son of Cyavana, whose body was filled with Śambhu's radiance, showed the entire cosmic egg within his own body. ॥37॥
2.2.39.38: Then Dadhīca, the best of Śaivas, the wise and fearless one, remembering Śaṅkara in his heart and laughing, spoke to Viṣṇu, the lord of gods. ॥38॥
2.2.39.39: Dadhīca said: What use is this illusion, or the power of mantras, O Hari? Making this a true resolve, you should fight with effort. ॥39॥
2.2.39.40: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of that sage, Viṣṇu, fearless then, became extremely angry with that sage, who was full of Śambhu's splendour. ॥40॥
2.2.39.41: And the gods again rushed forward, along with that god Nārāyaṇa, eager to fight with the mighty sage Dadhīca. ॥41॥
2.2.39.42: Meanwhile Kṣuva came there together with me, I the lotus-born, restraining Hari, who had been rendered powerless, and the gods. ॥42॥
2.2.39.43: Having heard my words that a brāhmaṇa cannot be conquered, Hari went near him and bowed to the sage. ॥43॥
2.2.39.44: Kṣuva, becoming most wretched, went there to Dadhīca, lord of sages, saluted him, and in distress entreated him. ॥44॥
2.2.39.45: Kṣuva said: Be gracious, O tiger among sages, crest-jewel of Śiva's devotees. Be gracious, O supreme lord, you who are ever hard for the wicked to perceive. ॥45॥
2.2.39.46: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of the king and of the host of gods, the brāhmaṇa Dadhīca, a treasury of austerities, showed favour to him. ॥46॥
2.2.39.47: Then, seeing Ramā's lord and the others, the sage, overcome with anger, remembering Śiva in his heart, cursed Viṣṇu and the gods as well. ॥47॥
2.2.39.48: Dadhīca said: O gods, together with Indra lord of gods, and O lords of sages, may you be destroyed by the fire of Rudra's wrath, along with the god Viṣṇu and your hosts. ॥48॥
2.2.39.49: Brahmā said: Having thus cursed the gods, the sage looked at Kṣuva and then said: O king of kings, the best of the twice-born is to be worshipped by the gods and by kings as well. ॥49॥
2.2.39.50: Brāhmaṇas alone, O king of kings, are strong and mighty. Having said this plainly, that brāhmaṇa entered his own hermitage. ॥50॥
2.2.39.51: Having saluted Dadhīca, Kṣuva went to his own home; Viṣṇu went with the gods to his own world, as he had come. ॥51॥
2.2.39.52: Thus that place became a sacred ford, remembered as Sthāneśvara; one who reaches Sthāneśvara would attain union with Śiva. ॥52॥
2.2.39.53: I have told you in brief, dear one, the dispute between Kṣuva and Dadhīca, and the story of Brahmā and Viṣṇu, who incurred a curse on the king's account, acting without Śiva. ॥53॥
2.2.39.54: Whoever recites daily this dispute between Kṣuva and Dadhīca, conquering untimely death, goes to Brahmaloka at the end of the body. ॥54॥
2.2.39.55: Whoever recites this and enters battle will never have fear of death, and he will be victorious. ॥55॥
2.2.39.iti: Thus ends the thirty-ninth adhyāya, named The description of the battle between Viṣṇu and Dadhīca, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥39॥
2.2.40.1: Nārada said: O Vidhi, O Vidhi, most wise one, revealer of the Śaiva truth, you have let me hear Śiva's most wonderful sport, which is utterly delightful. ॥1॥
2.2.40.2: When the heroic Vīrabhadra had destroyed Dakṣa's sacrifice and gone back to Mount Kailāsa, what happened then, dear father? Tell me that now. ॥2॥
2.2.40.3: Brahmā said: Then all the hosts of gods and the sages, defeated, their limbs wounded by Rudra's troops, went to my world. ॥3॥
2.2.40.4: Bowing to me, the Self-born, and praising me profusely, they reported their own distress in full detail. ॥4॥
2.2.40.5: Hearing that, I, afflicted by grief for my son, pondered, greatly agitated, with a tormented mind. ॥5॥
2.2.40.6: What should I do quickly today that brings happiness to the gods, by which that Dakṣa may live, the sacrifice be completed, and the gods be content? ॥6॥
2.2.40.7: Reflecting thus in many ways, O sage, I found no peace. Then, remembering Viṣṇu with devotion, I obtained the understanding appropriate to that moment. ॥7॥
2.2.40.8: Then, with the gods and sages, I went to Viṣṇu's world; bowing and praising him with various hymns, I told him of our grief. ॥8॥
2.2.40.9: O God, act so that the sacrifice may be completed, and he, the performer of the sacrifice may live, and all the gods and the sages may be happy. ॥9॥
2.2.40.10: O God of gods, Lord of Ramā, Viṣṇu, bringer of happiness to the gods, we, together with the gods and sages, have surely come to you for refuge. ॥10॥
2.2.40.11: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of mine, Brahmā, that Lord of Ramā, whose self is Śiva, remembering Śiva, replied with a sorrowful mind. ॥11॥
2.2.40.12: Viṣṇu said: For those who wish to prosper, an offence against one more powerful does not lead to welfare; in such a case the offenders' wish to thrive is fulfilled in many ways only by appeasing him. ॥12॥
2.2.40.13: All the gods have sinned against Śiva, the supreme Lord, since, O Vidhi, they withheld the sacrificial share of that Śambhu. ॥13॥
2.2.40.14: All of you, with pure minds, propitiate that Śiva of unsurpassed grace, clasping his two feet. ॥14॥
2.2.40.15: He is the god at whose anger the whole world perishes; seek quickly, by his command, the restoration to life of the sacrifice together with the world-guardians. ॥15॥
2.2.40.16: Quickly seek forgiveness from that god, who is bereft of his beloved and whose heart has been pierced by harsh words from the very wicked Dakṣa. ॥16॥
2.2.40.17: This alone, O Vidhi, is the great means to pacify him and to please Śambhu, I believe; what I have said is the truth. ॥17॥
2.2.40.18: Neither I, nor you, nor the other gods, nor even the sages and embodied beings know his true nature or the measure of his strength and valour. ॥18॥
2.2.40.19: Who would try to devise a scheme against that self-dependent, transcendent Supreme Self? Only an utterly deluded adversary. ॥19॥
2.2.40.20: I too, O Brahmā, will go with everyone to Śiva's abode and will surely seek forgiveness from Giriśa, for I too have offended against Śiva. ॥20॥
2.2.40.21: Brahmā said: Having thus instructed me, Brahmā, along with the gods and others, Viṣṇu resolved, together with the gods, to go to that mountain. ॥21॥
2.2.40.22: Hari, accompanied by the gods, sages, Prajāpatis and others, went to Kailāsa, the auspicious best of mountains, the dwelling of Śiva's own abode, ॥22॥
2.2.40.23: ever most dear to the Lord, well frequented by Kinnaras and others, by non-human beings, Apsarases and those perfected in yoga, and very lofty, ॥23॥
2.2.40.24: shining on all sides with peaks made of various gems, variegated with various minerals, and crowded with various trees and creepers, ॥24॥
2.2.40.25: filled with herds of various animals, endowed with various birds, with various springs of water, with the immortal lovers of the Siddha women ॥25॥
2.2.40.26: who sport there with their lovers, with various caves and slopes and with other kinds of trees — resplendent, shining like silver, ॥26॥
2.2.40.27: resounding with tigers and other great beasts yet free from cruelty, endowed with every beauty, divine, causing great wonder, ॥27॥
2.2.40.28: encircled by the Gaṅgā, whose waters are made holier by Satī's bathing at that place, she who purifies all, born from Viṣṇu's foot — exceedingly pure. ॥28॥
2.2.40.29: Seeing such a mountain, named Kailāsa, dear to Śiva, the gods headed by Viṣṇu, along with the great sages, were filled with wonder. ॥29॥
2.2.40.30: Near it the immortals saw the lovely city named Alakā, most divine, belonging to Kubera, the friend of Rudra. ॥30॥
2.2.40.31: Near it they also saw the Saugandhika forest, divine and full of all kinds of trees, where there is that wondrous sound. ॥31॥
2.2.40.32: Outside it were its two divine and most purifying rivers, Nandā and Alakanandā, which remove sin by their mere sight. ॥32॥
2.2.40.33: Celestial women, coming secretly from their own world, always drink their water; plunging in, they sport there with men, wearied by love-play. ॥33॥
2.2.40.34: Leaving behind the city of the lord of Yakṣas and the Saugandhika forest, the gods, going on, saw nearby Śaṅkara's banyan tree, ॥34॥
2.2.40.35: which cast a steady shade all around, whose branches spread over seventy-five yojanas, a hundred yojanas high, without nests, free from heat, ॥35॥
2.2.40.36: visible only to those of great merit, very lovely and most purifying, the divine place of Śambhu's yoga, resorted to by yogins, supremely excellent. ॥36॥
2.2.40.37: Beneath that banyan, refuge of those seeking liberation and full of great yoga, all the gods headed by Viṣṇu saw Śiva seated, ॥37॥
2.2.40.38: joyfully worshipped by Brahmā's sons, great Siddhas ever devoted to Śiva, tranquil, with completely calm forms, ॥38॥
2.2.40.39: and likewise especially attended always by his friend Kubera, lord of the Guhyakas and Rākṣasas, and by his own attendants and kinsmen, ॥39॥
2.2.40.40: the supreme Lord, bearing the true form cherished by ascetics, out of affection the friend of the universe, gloriously adorned with ash and the like. ॥40॥
2.2.40.41: O sage, they saw him well seated on a seat of kuśa grass, expounding the supreme knowledge to you, who were asking, while all the virtuous ones listened. ॥41॥
2.2.40.42: Having placed his left foot on the right thigh and the other on the knee, with a rosary on his forearm, he sat in the gesture of true reasoning (tarka-mudrā). ॥42॥
2.2.40.43: Seeing Śiva in this form, the gods headed by Viṣṇu then all quickly bowed down, humbly joining their hands. ॥43॥
2.2.40.44: Rudra, the refuge of the virtuous, perceiving that Viṣṇu had come with me, rose, and the Lord even saluted him with his head. ॥44॥
2.2.40.45: Then Śiva, whose feet had been saluted by all the divine ones headed by Viṣṇu, bowed in turn, just as Viṣṇu, the true refuge of the worlds, bows to Kaśyapa. ॥45॥
2.2.40.46: Śiva respectfully addressed Viṣṇu, who is well revered by the gods, siddhas, lords of the gaṇas and great sages, and who, together with the gods, had made obeisance. ॥46॥
2.2.40.iti: Thus ends the fortieth adhyāya, named The description of the sight of Śiva, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥40॥
2.2.41.1: Viṣṇu and the others said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, O Lord who follows worldly custom, by your grace we know you, Śambhu, the Lord, to be Brahman. ॥1॥
2.2.41.2: Why do you delude us, dear one, with your supreme māyā, which is always hard for men to understand and which bewilders them, O Supreme Lord? ॥2॥
2.2.41.3: You are the supreme Brahman, beyond Prakṛti and Puruṣa, the womb and the seed of the world, and beyond the reach of mind and speech. ॥3॥
2.2.41.4: You alone, by your own independent power, create, protect and devour the universe, sporting with Śiva-śakti, who is your own form, like a spider with its web. ॥4॥
2.2.41.5: You alone, O Īśāna, full of compassion, created the sacrifice, using Dakṣa as your instrument, O all-pervading one, for the constant upholding of the threefold Veda. ॥5॥
2.2.41.6: By you alone the boundaries of dharma have been set in the world, which brahmins firm in their vows and skilled in the Vedic path trust, knowing them to be pure. ॥6॥
2.2.41.7: For the doer of auspicious deeds you grant his own world or the highest in happiness, O Lord; and for the doers of inauspicious deeds, what is due — or a mixture, or the reverse. ॥7॥
2.2.41.8: You alone are always the giver of the fruits of all actions. All beings are declared to be paśus, and you are their lord, as heard in the Śruti. ॥8॥
2.2.41.9: Those of divisive minds, who see only ritual action, who wound others to the quick and are evil-hearted — these fools, filled with envy, torment others with harsh words. ॥9॥
2.2.41.10: O Lord, for those already struck down by fate, let there not be slaying by you as well. Blessed one, supreme Īśāna, show mercy, O highest Lord. ॥10॥
2.2.41.11: Salutation to Rudra, the peaceful, to Brahman, the supreme Self; salutation to the wearer of matted locks, to Maheśa, the radiant, the great. ॥11॥
2.2.41.12: You are the creator of the creators of the universe; you are the sustainer, the great-grandsire; you are of the three guṇas and also beyond the guṇas, higher than Prakṛti and Puruṣa. ॥12॥
2.2.41.13: Salutation to you, the blue-throated, the ordainer, the supreme Self, the universe, the seed of the universe, the cause of the world's joy. ॥13॥
2.2.41.14: You are the syllable Om and the call vaṣaṭ, the one who sets every undertaking in motion; the call hanta and the call svadhā, always the eater of offerings to the gods, to the ancestors, and of food. ॥14॥
2.2.41.15: How was the sacrifice destroyed by you, O one devoted to dharma? You are devoted to brahmins, O Mahādeva; how could you be the destroyer of the sacrifice, O Lord? ॥15॥
2.2.41.16: You are the protector of brahmins, of cows, and of dharma; you are the refuge, ever infinite, of all living beings, O Lord. ॥16॥
2.2.41.17: Salutation to you, Blessed Rudra, whose brilliance surpasses the sun's beyond measure. Salutation to you, Bhava, the god, who are taste (rasa), consisting of water. ॥17॥
2.2.41.18: Salutation to Śarva, whose form is the earth, ever fragrant. Salutation to Rudra, whose nature is fire, of great brilliance. ॥18॥
2.2.41.19: Salutation again and again to you, Īśa, the wind, who are touch. Salutation to you, lord of creatures, the sacrificer, the ordainer. ॥19॥
2.2.41.20: Salutation to you, Bhīma, whose form is space, who are sound alone. Salutation be to you, Mahādeva, Soma, the active one. ॥20॥
2.2.41.21: Salutation to you, Ugra, whose form is the sun, the yogin of action. Salutation to you, death of Death; salutation to you, wrath of Rudra. ॥21॥
2.2.41.22: Salutation to you, Śiva, Bhīma, Śaṅkara, Śiva. You are fierce, the controller of all beings, yet you are auspicious to us. ॥22॥
2.2.41.23: To the bestower of happiness, the universe, Brahman, the destroyer of affliction; salutation to you, lord of Ambikā, lord of Umā. ॥23॥
2.2.41.24: To Śarva, of all forms, the Puruṣa, the supreme Self, free of manifestation as being or non-being, the cause of Mahat — to you salutation. ॥24॥
2.2.41.25: Salutation again and again to the one born in many ways in the world, the abundant. To the Blue one, Nīlarudra, Kadrudra, the wise. ॥25॥
2.2.41.26: Salutation to you, the most bountiful, the god, Śipiviṣṭa. Salutation to you, the greatest, ever the slayer of the enemies of the gods. ॥26॥
2.2.41.27: Salutation again and again to Tāra and Sutāra, the youthful, of fine brilliance, to Harikeśa, the god, Maheśa. ॥27॥
2.2.41.28: To you, Śambhu of the gods, the all-pervading, the supreme Self; salutation to you, the supreme; salutation to you, the dark-throated. ॥28॥
2.2.41.29: Salutation to the golden one, the supreme Lord, golden-bodied; to the terrible one, of terrible form, delighting in terrible deeds. ॥29॥
2.2.41.30: To the one whose body is smeared with ash and who is adorned with rudrākṣa; salutation to the short, the tall; salutation be to you, the dwarf. ॥30॥
2.2.41.31: Salutation again and again to you, O god, who slay from afar and who slay in front. Salutation to you, bearer of the bow, the trident, the mace, the plough. ॥31॥
2.2.41.32: To the bearer of many weapons, destroyer of Daityas and Dānavas; salutation indeed to Sadya, of the form of Sadya, to Sadyojāta. ॥32॥
2.2.41.33: Salutation to you, Vāma, of beautiful form, of beautiful eyes. Salutation again and again to Aghora, the supreme Lord, the formidable. ॥33॥
2.2.41.34: To Tatpuruṣa, the Lord, and the ancient Puruṣa; to the giver of the aims of human life, the observer of vows, Parameṣṭhin. ॥34॥
2.2.41.35: Salutation to you, Īśāna; salutation again and again to Īśvara; salutation to Brahman, of the form of Brahman, the supreme Self in person. ॥35॥
2.2.41.36: You are fierce, the controller of all the wicked; you are auspicious to us. Salutation to you, the swallower of the Kālakūṭa poison, the protector of the gods and others. ॥36॥
2.2.41.37: Salutation to the hero, Vīrabhadra, protector of heroes, the trident-bearer; to Mahādeva, the great, the lord of creatures. ॥37॥
2.2.41.38: To the heroic-souled, the one of excellent knowledge, Śrīkaṇṭha, the bearer of Pināka; salutation to the endless, the subtle; salutation to you, the wrath that is death to death. ॥38॥
2.2.41.39: To the supreme, the supreme Lord, higher than the highest; salutation to you, the highest beyond the highest, the all-pervading, whose form is the universe. ॥39॥
2.2.41.40: Salutation to the one whose consort is Viṣṇu, whose field is Viṣṇu, the sun; to Bhairava, the refuge, Tryambaka, the one who sports. ॥40॥
2.2.41.41: To Mṛtyuñjaya (the conqueror of death), to the one who is grief to the wicked, to the one possessing the three guṇas, to the one whose self is the guṇas, to the one whose eyes are the moon, the sun and fire, to the bridge that is the ground of all causes — salutations. ॥41॥
2.2.41.42: For the whole world is pervaded by you through your own splendour. You are the supreme Brahman, changeless, consciousness and bliss, luminous. ॥42॥
2.2.41.43: All the gods, headed by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra, Candra and others, and the other sages too, have been born from you, O Maheśvara. ॥43॥
2.2.41.44: Since you sustain everything by dividing your body eightfold, you are called Aṣṭamūrti; and you are the Lord, the primordial one, full of compassion. ॥44॥
2.2.41.45: From fear of you this wind blows; from fear of you fire burns; through fear of you the sun gives heat; and death runs about everywhere. ॥45॥
2.2.41.46: O ocean of compassion, O Maheśāna, be gracious, O supreme Lord. Protect, protect us always, since we are ruined and bewildered. ॥46॥
2.2.41.47: We have constantly been protected by you alone, O Lord, O treasure of compassion, from various calamities, O Śambhu; likewise protect us today. ॥47॥
2.2.41.48: O Lord, bestower of grace, quickly bring about the restoration of the unfinished sacrifice of Dakṣa the Prajāpati, O Durgeśa. ॥48॥
2.2.41.49: May Bhaga regain his eyes, and may the sacrificer live; may Pūṣan's teeth grow again, and Bhṛgu's beard be as before. ॥49॥
2.2.41.50: And, O Śaṅkara, may there be health for the gods and others, favoured by you, whose limbs have been entirely shattered by weapons and stones. ॥50॥
2.2.41.51: O Lord, let there be a full share for you in the remaining sacrificial rite. The sacrifice shall be arranged for you with Rudra's share, never otherwise anywhere. ॥51॥
2.2.41.52: Having spoken thus, that Lord of creatures (Brahmā) and the Lord of Ramā (Viṣṇu), with joined palms, fell prostrate on the ground like a staff, intent on seeking forgiveness. ॥52॥
2.2.41.iti: Thus ends the forty-first adhyāya, named The description of the praise by the gods, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥41॥
2.2.42.1: Brahmā said: Entreated by the glorious Brahmā, lord of creatures, and constantly by the sage as well, Śambhu, the supreme Lord, became gracious. ॥1॥
2.2.42.2: Having reassured the gods headed by Viṣṇu, the supreme Lord, treasure of compassion, smiled and spoke, bestowing supreme grace. ॥2॥
2.2.42.3: Śrī Mahādeva said: Listen attentively to my words, O two best of gods. I tell you both the truth, dear ones: I have always borne your anger. ॥3॥
2.2.42.4: I neither speak of nor dwell upon the sin of those who are like children in their person; on those overcome by my māyā, the punishment there was inflicted by me. ॥4॥
2.2.42.5: This destruction of Dakṣa's sacrifice was in no way done by me. When one hates another, what one intends for others will befall oneself. ॥5॥
2.2.42.6: An act that harms others should never be done. When one hates another, what one intends for others will befall oneself. ॥6॥
2.2.42.7: Let Dakṣa, whose head was offered in the sacrifice, have a goat-faced head; let the god Bhaga see his share of the sacrifice through the eye of Mitra. ॥7॥
2.2.42.8: The god named Pūṣan, dear one, whose teeth were broken, shall eat ground flour with the teeth of the sacrificer; this I have declared truly. ॥8॥
2.2.42.9: Bhṛgu, who opposed me, shall indeed have a goat's beard. The gods who gave me the remnant of the offering shall have all their limbs restored to their natural state. ॥9॥
2.2.42.10: Let the other adhvaryu priests be provided with arms made from the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan; this I have spoken out of affection for you. ॥10॥
2.2.42.11: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, the supreme Lord, full of compassion, fell silent — the god, lord of the moving and unmoving, the sovereign who acts in accordance with the Veda. ॥11॥
2.2.42.12: Then all the gods and the rest, together with Viṣṇu and Brahmā, hearing Śaṅkara's words, were fully satisfied and exclaimed, excellent, excellent. ॥12॥
2.2.42.13: Then, having invited Śambhu, Viṣṇu, with me and the gods and sages, went once more with great joy to that place of sacrifice. ॥13॥
2.2.42.14: Thus, at the request of the gods headed by Viṣṇu, Śambhu went to Kanakhala, to the sacrificial enclosure of the Prajāpati. ॥14॥
2.2.42.15: Then Rudra saw there the destruction of the sacrifice wrought by Vīrabhadra, especially that inflicted on the gods and sages. ॥15॥
2.2.42.16: Svāhā, Svadhā, Pūṣan, Tuṣṭi, Dhṛti, Sarasvatī, and likewise all the other sages, the Pitṛs and the Fires, ॥16॥
2.2.42.17: and the many others there — Yakṣas, Gandharvas and Rākṣasas — had been torn and plucked apart, and some had died on the battlefield. ॥17॥
2.2.42.18: Seeing the sacrifice in such a state, the Lord summoned the mighty Vīrabhadra, chief of the gaṇas, and spoke to him, laughing. ॥18॥
2.2.42.19: O mighty-armed Vīrabhadra, what is this deed you have done? Dear one, you have swiftly inflicted a great punishment on the gods, sages and others. ॥19॥
2.2.42.20: Bring Dakṣa quickly, by whom this sacrifice was performed in such a manner — a strange sacrifice indeed, dear one, whose fruit is such as this. ॥20॥
2.2.42.21: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by Śaṅkara, Vīrabhadra hastily brought the headless trunk and threw it down before Śambhu. ॥21॥
2.2.42.22: Seeing him headless, Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, smiling, spoke to Vīrabhadra before him, O best of sages. ॥22॥
2.2.42.23: When he asked where the head was, the lordly Vīrabhadra said: I offered the head into the fire at that very moment, O Śaṅkara. ॥23॥
2.2.42.24: Hearing these words of Vīrabhadra, Lord Śaṅkara kindly commanded the gods accordingly, as he had said before. ॥24॥
2.2.42.25: Having carried out completely what the blessed Bhava had said, Viṣṇu and all the others, with me, then quickly restored Bhṛgu and the rest. ॥25॥
2.2.42.26: Then, by Śambhu's gracious command, they swiftly joined to the body of that Prajāpati the head of the goat that was the animal for the soma-pressing. ॥26॥
2.2.42.27: As the head was being joined, the Prajāpati, looked upon by Śambhu's gracious glance, at once regained his life and rose up as if from sleep. ॥27॥
2.2.42.28: Having risen, Dakṣa saw before him Śambhu, the treasure of compassion; with a delighted heart and a mind fully serene, he stood there in affection. ॥28॥
2.2.42.29: Formerly his soul had been sullied by great hatred of Hara; at the sight of Śiva he at once became spotless like the autumn moon. ॥29॥
2.2.42.30: Then, though he wished to praise Bhava, he could not, because of his overwhelming love and his agitation from longing, as he remembered his departed daughter. ॥30॥
2.2.42.31: Then Dakṣa, his heart serene and filled with shame, bowed down and praised Śiva, Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds. ॥31॥
2.2.42.32: Dakṣa said: I bow to the god, giver of boons, most worthy of choice, the great Lord, treasure of knowledge, eternal. I bow to Hara, lord over the sovereigns of the gods, ever full of bliss, the sole kinsman of the world. ॥32॥
2.2.42.33: O Lord of the universe, I bow to you whose form is the universe, the ancient one, whose own essential form is Brahman. I bow to Śarva, the source of existence and being; to Śaṅkara, higher than the highest, I am bowed down. ॥33॥
2.2.42.34: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, show mercy; salutation to you. Forgive my offence today, O Śambhu, treasure of compassion. ॥34॥
2.2.42.35: Indeed, O Śaṅkara, you have bestowed grace under the guise of punishment. I am wicked and dull-witted, O God; I did not know your true nature. ॥35॥
2.2.42.36: Today I have known the truth: you are held to be above all, the great Lord, to be served by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and others, knowable through the Vedas. ॥36॥
2.2.42.37: You are the wish-fulfilling tree for the good and ever the wielder of the rod for the wicked; you are independent, the supreme Self, granting the boons desired by devotees. ॥37॥
2.2.42.38: You, the supreme Lord, first created from your mouth the twice-born, bearers of learning, austerity and vows, so that they might fully know the truth of the Self. ॥38॥
2.2.42.39: You protect them from all calamities as a herdsman protects his cattle; rod in hand against those wicked ones, you are the guardian of the bounds of right conduct. ॥39॥
2.2.42.40: The supreme Lord, though pierced by me with the arrows of harsh words, is the bestower of grace upon me and upon the gods whose hopes were utterly wretched. ॥40॥
2.2.42.41: Such are you, the Lord, O Śambhu, friend of the afflicted, higher than the highest; O you who are affectionate to your devotees, you are pleased by your own most worthy deed. ॥41॥
2.2.42.42: Brahmā said: Having thus praised the great lord Śaṅkara, who brings welfare to the worlds, the Prajāpati Dakṣa, humble in spirit, fell silent before the great Lord. ॥42॥
2.2.42.43: Then Viṣṇu, gladdened in heart, having bowed deeply with joined palms, praised the bull-bannered Śiva in a voice choked with tears. ॥43॥
2.2.42.44: Viṣṇu said: O Mahādeva, great lord, bestower of grace on the worlds, you are the supreme Brahman, the supreme Self, O friend of the afflicted, O treasury of compassion. ॥44॥
2.2.42.45: O Lord, you are all-pervading, acting by your own will, whose glory is to be known through the Vedas. By this you have shown grace, and we have been made well-doers. ॥45॥
2.2.42.46: This Dakṣa is my devotee; that the wicked one formerly reviled you—that should be forgiven, O great lord, today, since you are free from all change. ॥46॥
2.2.42.47: I too committed an offence against you, O Śaṅkara, out of folly, in that I fought with your attendant Vīrabhadra by taking Dakṣa's side. ॥47॥
2.2.42.48: You are my master, the supreme Brahman; I am your servant, O Sadāśiva, and ever to be sustained by you, for you are the father of all. ॥48॥
2.2.42.49: Brahmā said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, ocean of compassion, Lord, you are independent, the supreme Self, the supreme lord, without a second, imperishable. ॥49॥
2.2.42.50: O God, O Īśvara, you have shown grace to my son. Disregarding the insult to yourself, restore Dakṣa's sacrifice. ॥50॥
2.2.42.51: Be gracious, O lord of the gods, and remove all curses. You, with knowledge, are my inspirer, and you alone are the one who restrains. ॥51॥
2.2.42.52: Having thus praised the supreme great lord, O great sage, I stood with palms joined in a cup and head bowed low. ॥52॥
2.2.42.53: Then the gods headed by Śakra, the guardians of the worlds, pure-minded, praised the god Śaṅkara, whose lotus face was gracious. ॥53॥
2.2.42.54: Then all the gods, glad at heart, and others as well—the Siddhas, the sages and the Prajāpatis—joyfully praised Śaṅkara. ॥54॥
2.2.42.55: Likewise the demigods and Nāgas, the members of the assembly and the brāhmaṇas, bowing with supreme devotion, praised him each separately. ॥55॥
2.2.42.iti: Thus ends the forty-second adhyāya, named The description of the removal of Dakṣa's suffering, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥42॥
2.2.43.1: Brahmā said: Thus praised by Viṣṇu, the lord of Ramā, by me, by the divine sages, and likewise by others, Mahādeva became gracious. ॥1॥
2.2.43.2: Then Śambhu, having reassured with his compassionate glance all the sages, gods and others, as well as Brahmā and Viṣṇu, spoke this to Dakṣa. ॥2॥
2.2.43.3: Mahādeva said: Listen, Dakṣa, I shall speak; I am pleased, O Prajāpati. Though independent and lord of all, I am always subject to my devotees. ॥3॥
2.2.43.4: Four kinds of virtuous people always worship me, O Dakṣa, O Prajāpati; among them each succeeding one is superior to the one before. ॥4॥
2.2.43.5: The distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the knower as the fourth: the first three are ordinary, but the fourth is distinguished. ॥5॥
2.2.43.6: Of them the knower is dearest to me and is considered my very form. None is dearer than him; truly, truly I say this. ॥6॥
2.2.43.7: I, the knower of the Self, am to be reached through knowledge by those who have mastered the Vedānta scriptures; yet the dull-witted strive to attain me without knowledge. ॥7॥
2.2.43.8: Not by the Vedas, nor by sacrifices, nor by gifts, nor ever by austerity are deluded men bound by ritual action able to attain me. ॥8॥
2.2.43.9: You wished to cross worldly existence by ritual action alone; for that very reason I became angry and caused the destruction of the sacrifice. ॥9॥
2.2.43.10: From now on, O Dakṣa, regarding me as the supreme Lord, become devoted to knowledge through understanding and perform your actions with a collected mind. ॥10॥
2.2.43.11: Hear also another word of mine with a good mind, O Prajāpati: for the sake of dharma I tell you a secret, even about my aspect with attributes. ॥11॥
2.2.43.12: I, Brahmā and Viṣṇu are the supreme cause of the world; I am the Self, the Lord, the witness, self-seeing and without distinguishing attributes. ॥12॥
2.2.43.13: Entering my own Māyā, which consists of the guṇas, O sage, I, that very one, creating, protecting and withdrawing the universe, bear names suited to those functions. ॥13॥
2.2.43.14: In that supreme, non-dual, sole Brahman, the Self, the ignorant one sees beings, Brahmā and the Lord as separate. ॥14॥
2.2.43.15: Just as a person never thinks of his own limbs such as head and hands as belonging to another, so one devoted to me never regards beings as other. ॥15॥
2.2.43.16: He who sees no difference among the three gods, who are of one essence and are the selves of all beings, O Dakṣa, attains peace. ॥16॥
2.2.43.17: The vilest of men who conceives of difference among the three gods will surely dwell in hell as long as the moon and stars endure. ॥17॥
2.2.43.18: The discerning person devoted to me should worship all the gods too; he obtains the knowledge by which liberation becomes everlasting. ॥18॥
2.2.43.19: Without devotion to Brahmā, devotion to Viṣṇu does not arise at all; and without devotion to Viṣṇu, devotion to me never arises anywhere. ॥19॥
2.2.43.20: Having said this, Śaṅkara, the master and supreme Lord of all, the abode of compassion, spoke these words there while everyone listened. ॥20॥
2.2.43.21: If a devotee of Hari should revile me, or likewise a Śaiva should revile Hari, those curses would fall on both of them, and they would never attain the truth. ॥21॥
2.2.43.22: Brahmā said: Hearing these delightful words of Maheśa, all the gods, sages and others there rejoiced, O sage. ॥22॥
2.2.43.23: Then Dakṣa with his family, in great joy, became devoted to Śiva; and the gods and others, too, regarded Śiva as the lord of all. ॥23॥
2.2.43.24: In whatever way each one had praised Śambhu, the supreme Self, in that way Śambhu, pleased at heart, granted him a boon. ॥24॥
2.2.43.25: Permitted quickly by Śiva, Dakṣa, now a devotee of Śiva and serene in mind, completed the sacrifice through Śiva's grace, O sage. ॥25॥
2.2.43.26: He gave the gods their shares and the full share to Śiva; he also gave gifts to the brāhmaṇas, and Śambhu's grace was obtained. ॥26॥
2.2.43.27: Then Dakṣa the Prajāpati, together with the officiating priests, duly completed that very great rite for the god, performed according to the injunctions. ॥27॥
2.2.43.28: Thus Dakṣa's sacrifice was completed there, O lord of sages, through the grace of Śaṅkara, whose form is the supreme Brahman. ॥28॥
2.2.43.29: Then all the gods and sages, extolling Śaṅkara's glory, went contentedly to their own abodes, and the others too went happily. ॥29॥
2.2.43.30: Viṣṇu and I too, greatly pleased, went joyfully each to our own supreme abode, ever singing the fair glory of Śambhu, which bestows every auspiciousness. ॥30॥
2.2.43.31: Mahādeva too, the refuge of the good, honoured lovingly by Dakṣa, went, well pleased, with his gaṇas to his own mountain Kailāsa. ॥31॥
2.2.43.32: Having reached his own mountain, Śambhu remembered his beloved Satī and told her story to the gaṇas, especially the chief ones. ॥32॥
2.2.43.33: The all-knowing Lord passed much time recounting her deeds, adopting the way of the world and displaying the state of a lover. ॥33॥
2.2.43.34: The master, who never acts improperly, is the supreme Brahman, the goal of the good; where, then, is delusion for him, or grief, or any other change, O sage? ॥34॥
2.2.43.35: Viṣṇu and I never know his secret; what then of other sages, gods, humans and yogins? ॥35॥
2.2.43.36: Śaṅkara's greatness is infinite and hard for the wise to comprehend; it is known to devotees through true devotion, by his grace, without toil. ॥36॥
2.2.43.37: Śiva, the supreme Self, has not even a single change; he shows such a condition to the worlds by assuming it. ॥37॥
2.2.43.38: By reading and hearing this, O sage, any wise person among all people attains a divine, blessed destiny and supreme happiness even here. ॥38॥
2.2.43.39: Thus Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, having given up her body, was born again of Menā, the wife of Himavat; so it is well known. ॥39॥
2.2.43.40: Performing austerities there once more, she chose Śiva as her husband; becoming Gaurī, the left half of his body, Śivā performed wondrous sports. ॥40॥
2.2.43.41: Thus the supremely wondrous story of Satī has been described to you — divine, bestowing worldly enjoyment and liberation, and granting all desires. ॥41॥
2.2.43.42: This narrative is sinless, pure, supremely purifying; it leads to heaven, brings fame and long life, and yields the fruit of sons and grandsons. ॥42॥
2.2.43.43: Whoever listens to this with devotion, or, being devoted, makes other people hear it, O dear one, attains the fruit of all rites and reaches the supreme state in the next world. ॥43॥
2.2.43.44: Whoever reads this auspicious narrative, or has it read, he too, having enjoyed all pleasures, would attain liberation at the end. ॥44॥
2.2.43.iti: Thus ends the forty-third adhyāya, named The description of the setting in order of Dakṣa's sacrifice, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥43॥
